### SEC-113 — Electron renderer runs with NO Content-Security-Policy (Electron security warning; XSS exposure)

- **Category:** SECURITY  |  **Severity:** Medium  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-01, 17th session)
- **Repositories:** AgentGithubUplaod (desktop)
- **Platforms affected:** Desktop (Electron renderer)
- **Task:** T-108 (owner-reported evidence, 17th session)
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-01 — the owner pasted the desktop's dev console showing `Electron Security Warning (Insecure Content-Security-Policy): This renderer process has either no Content-Security-Policy set or a policy with "unsafe-eval" enabled.` `index.html` had carried NO CSP meta since its first commit.
- **Risk:** without a CSP the renderer's XSS blast radius is unmitigated (any injected script executes with full DOM + localStorage/session access — the session storage holds the Supabase JWT).
- **What was changed:** a CSP meta added to `elimtiyaz-desktop/index.html` (applies in dev AND packaged modes). Policy: `script-src 'self'` (no unsafe-eval/unsafe-inline); `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com` (the design system renders inline style ATTRIBUTES — blocking them breaks the UI; style-attr injection is not an XSS vector); `font-src` Google Fonts; `img-src 'self' data: blob: https:` (media vault + Supabase storage); `connect-src 'self' https: wss: ws://localhost:* http://localhost:*` (the app connects to a USER-CONFIGURED Supabase project URL — arbitrary host, TLS-only outbound; localhost ws for Vite dev HMR); `worker-src 'self' blob:` (particle engine image loader); `object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`.
- **Verification:** production launch under Xvfb (25s alive): zero security warnings, zero CSP violations, only the documented container dbus/GPU noise (T-097 baseline); dev-mode launch against the Vite dev server (30s, devtools open): zero security warnings, zero violations, no failed resource loads. NEW `src/tests/security/csp-policy.test.ts` 4/4 pins the security-critical properties (script-src self-only; object/frame-ancestors/base-uri hardening; the functional allowances) so the policy cannot silently regress. Desktop suite/typecheck/lint green (counts in the change-log).
- **Residual:** `connect-src https:` is deliberately broad (the Configuration tab accepts any project URL — a functional requirement); the CSP's warning class is suppressed in packaged builds anyway, but the policy now also holds there.

### ARCH-013 — Migration 0065 applied to the live DB by an actor outside the repos (2nd ARCH-011-class event: live SQL with no committed file, no task, no problem entry)

- **Category:** ARCH  |  **Severity:** High  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-02, 19th session — drift closed by reconstruction + verification; the PROCESS gap itself remains owner-side)
- **Repositories:** AgentGithubUplaod (hub, backend chain owner)
- **Platforms affected:** Backend/DB, all three clients (typed RPC surface)
- **Task:** T-115 (docs/recovery/task-registry.md) · full evidence: docs/recovery/t-115-live-verification.md
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-02, 19th-session opening check (the mandated live-chain diff): live `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` returned 62 rows — the committed chain's 61 (0001–0064) PLUS `0065 / canonical_identity_codes`, registered after the 18th-session close (2026-09-01 ~04:31 UTC). No `0065_*.sql` file, no task entry, no problem entry, no commit existed in ANY of the three repositories; the live function bodies self-cite a task ID ("T-115") that was never registered in the task registry.
- **Root cause:** an actor (previous agent session or owner-side tool) applied DDL to the live project via the Management API WITHOUT following the MIG-TOKENS discipline's documentation half (commit the file, register the task, update the registries). This is the same class as ARCH-011 (0053/0054, 2026-08-31) — the class recurs because applying live SQL is technically one curl call while the repo-side bookkeeping is where the discipline lives.
- **Risk:** a fresh deployment (`db push`) from the repos would have silently MISSED the four canonical identity-code functions + the batch_register_family rewrite — the live system and any rebuilt system would diverge at the identity-code layer (the exact layer the (tenant_id, parent_code) idempotency contract depends on). Additionally the unregistered "T-115" citation in live SQL was drift bait: the next agent would find a task ID that resolves to nothing.
- **What was done (19th session):** the migration was reconstructed VERBATIM from the live catalog (pg_get_functiondef; one-time file-vs-live comparison: 5/5 definitions byte-identical), committed as `elimtiyaz-desktop/supabase/migrations/0065_canonical_identity_codes.sql`, applied live atomically via the standard MIG-TOKENS script (idempotent CREATE OR REPLACE + registration ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING — the pre-existing row preserved), live-verified 19/19 (`scripts/verify_t-115.sql`), task T-115 registered, this entry written, and the cross-platform surface aligned (typed RPCs registered in desktop types.ts + website database.ts; desktop TS ↔ SQL equivalence pinned by a 9-test suite; the mock layer + the approve-signup-request EF aligned to the now-deterministic server contract).
- **Residual (owner-side):** identify the actor/process that applied 0065 without committing it — if it was an agent session, its session artifacts (wherever they live) should be reconciled or discarded; if it was a dashboard/tool action, the owner should route future schema changes through the hub repo (ADR-001: the hub chain is the ONLY schema source of truth). The live-vs-file cosmetic comment gap (Management API drops COMMENT ON — see the live-verification doc §5) is documented and accepted.
- **Verification:** docs/recovery/t-115-live-verification.md (file==live 5/5; verify_t-115.sql 19/19; desktop 75 files / 2236 tests; leak checks 0/259/0).

### ACT-201 — Production portal requested `/undefined/functions/v1/bind-activation-code` → 404 on every activation attempt (owner-reported console evidence)

- **Category:** AUTH  |  **Severity:** Critical  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-05, 28th session — T-184; URL-routing live-verified)
- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-website
- **Platforms affected:** Website (activation screen — production Vercel deployment)
- **Task:** T-184
- **Consolidated from:** owner report 2026-09-05 (browser console: `/undefined/functions/v1/bind-activation-code` 404 + the Firebase env warning paste)
- **Description:** `activation-code-screen.tsx` built the Edge Function URL from a DIRECT runtime read of the build-time env var (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`) inside a `"use client"` component. Next.js inlines `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values at BUILD time — the production Vercel project had NOT set them (the same session paste shows the FCM env warning, i.e. NO `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` vars are configured on the host), so the inlined value was `undefined` and the browser requested `undefined/functions/v1/bind-activation-code` as a RELATIVE path on the PORTAL origin → 404 from the portal's own server/CDN. Every activation attempt failed no matter how valid the code was. The live EF itself was healthy the whole time (anon probes 2026-09-05: POST with publishable-key apikey → the EF's own structured 401 `{"error":{"code":"unauthorized"}}`; OPTIONS → 200; garbage Bearer → 401 `auth_failed`). The portal otherwise worked because the `supabase` browser client (`src/lib/supabase/client.ts`) already resolves through `@/lib/env` with the T-096 committed fallback — this one screen was the ONLY direct `process.env` reader in client code.
- **Resolution:** T-184 — the screen now imports `env` from `@/lib/env` and builds `${env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL}/functions/v1/bind-activation-code` with `apikey: env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (fallback chain: build-time env vars → committed `PUBLIC_CONFIG_DEFAULTS`). The T-153 structured-error mapping (`mapActivationError(data)`) is untouched. Permanent rule added to the website AGENTS.md §5 (never read `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_*` directly in a client component) + a whole-src regression test that fails if any non-`env.ts` file does.
- **Verification:** website suite 28 files / 483 tests (7 new T-184 tests: no direct env reads anywhere in src, `@/lib/env` import pinned, fresh-clone fallback equals the committed default, URL well-formed against the shared project, T-153 contract preserved); `npm run lint` clean; strict `npm run build` green. Live: the exact request the fixed client emits (publishable-key apikey, no auth) now reaches the REAL EF → structured 401 (routing proven end-to-end; the authenticated happy path was already live-verified by T-147's 19/19 round-trip).
- **Left:** owner-side deploy step — rebuild/redeploy the portal on Vercel with this code (the fix is code-level and needs no env vars, but the running deployment must be updated). Optional hardening: setting `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` + `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` as Vercel env vars also works (override semantics). The Firebase env-vars warning in the same console paste is the DOCUMENTED truthful state (AUTH-202/T-121: web app id + VAPID key never issued — web push disabled by design until the owner supplies them; NOT a defect).

### ACT-202 — Desktop `bindActivationCode` collapsed every EF failure into the generic "Function returned an error" (structured body unreachable)

- **Category:** AUTH  |  **Severity:** Medium  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-05, 28th session — T-184)
- **Repositories:** AgentGithubUplaod (desktop infrastructure layer)
- **Platforms affected:** desktop (staff-assisted binding / test surface for bind-activation-code)
- **Task:** T-184
- **Consolidated from:** owner report 2026-09-05 ("Fix both the desktop app and the website") — the desktop half of the activation-code mandate.
- **Description:** `SupabaseApprovalRepository.bindActivationCode` consumed `functions.invoke`'s `{ data, error }` as if a non-2xx body landed in `data` — but `@supabase/functions-js` (2.112.3, verified in node_modules: `return { data: null, error, response }` for every non-2xx) wraps the raw Response in `FunctionsHttpError` whose `message` is the generic "Function returned an error". The hub EF's structured body `{ error: { code, message } }` (the `_shared/cors.ts` jsonError shape, pinned by T-146/T-147) never reached the `data` channel, so the staff could not distinguish invalid code / expired / already-bound family / already-active from a server fault. (The website got the precise mapping in T-153; the desktop never had the equivalent.)
- **Resolution:** T-184 — new `structuredEdgeFunctionError()` helper parses the structured body off `error.context` (the raw Response); `bindActivationCode` maps the EF codes to precise AppErrors: `account_already_active` → ERR_CONFLICT (idempotent per ADR-011), `parent_already_bound` → ERR_CONFLICT, `code_not_found` / `code_expired` → ERR_VALIDATION with the EF's real message + French userMessage, `account_suspended` / `account_rejected` → ERR_FORBIDDEN, others → ERR_SERVER; context-less errors (network class) and non-JSON bodies still fall back to the unchanged generic mapping. The `{ data: { data } }` jsonOk unwrap contract is preserved.
- **Verification:** desktop 10 new tests (`src/tests/infrastructure/t-184-bind-activation-structured-errors.test.ts`: body key `activation_code` pinned, jsonOk unwrap, all 5 EF code mappings, network fallback, non-JSON fallback, local 6–7-digit short-circuit); t-145 (5/5) + t-146 canonical EF (8/8) re-run green; full desktop suite 86 files / 2371 tests / 0 failures; `tsc --noEmit` clean; lint 0 errors.
- **Left:** nothing agent-side; the method has no UI caller yet (it is the repository surface for the staff-assisted bind / test harness) — when a UI lands it inherits the precise errors.

### ACT-201-related owner note — the Firebase env warning in the same console paste is NOT a defect

- **Category:** AUTH  |  **Severity:** Info  |  **Status:** Documented truthful state (T-121, 2026-09-02; no action taken — owner-gated)
- **Description:** The owner's 2026-09-05 console paste included `[env] Firebase env vars incomplete — push notifications will be disabled. Missing: NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID (the WEB app id), NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_VAPID_KEY.` This is the T-121/AUTH-202 warning working AS DESIGNED: the known Firebase app id is the ANDROID app id (a different app in the same Firebase project) and no web-push VAPID key has ever been issued, so web push stays disabled and the warning names the exact two vars to set. The warning then goes quiet and `isFcmConfigured` flips true.

### DATA-015 — Itemization attribution gap: family-level charges could vanish from the "shopping list" (single-child fold bug)

- **Category:** DATA  |  **Severity:** Medium  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-05, 27th session — T-168/T-169/T-170, all three platforms)
- **Repositories:** AgentGithubUplaod (desktop engine), elimtiyaz-website (canonical port), elimtiyaz-android (core mirror)
- **Platforms affected:** all three (the canonical engine + both mirrors shared the attribution rule)
- **Task:** T-168 (desktop), T-169 (website), T-170 (Android)
- **Description:** the per-child itemization only folded family-level (null `student_id`) charge rows into the child when the child had ZERO direct charges. A single-child family with direct charges PLUS family-level rows (e.g. 285 000 tuition attributed to the child + a 40 000 family-level registration fee) rendered `billedTotal = 285 000` while `totalBilled = 325 000` — the 40 000 appeared in NO itemized view (mystery money, the exact class the owner asked to eliminate). Multi-child families were already explicit (T-168 adds the "Famille — éléments non rattachés" block), so only the single-child partial-attribution case was affected.
- **Resolution:** single-child families now ALWAYS own the family-level rows (direct charges + null-studentId rows merged, mirroring the installments attribution rule); the new conservation invariant is pinned by tests on all three platforms: Σ byChild.billedTotal + unattributedTotal === totalBilled.
- **Verification:** the 700 000 DZD 2-child corpus (2×285 000 tuition + 2×45 000 transport + 40 000 family-level) and the single-child 325 000 fold case pass on desktop (28/28), website (19/19) and Android (19/19) suites.
- **Left:** nothing — historical rows need no repair (the gap was read-side only; the ledger always balanced).

### PARITY-001 — Cross-platform mirror rounding hazard: Kotlin integer division silently diverges from TS Math.round

- **Category:** CROSS (parity hazard)  |  **Severity:** Low (caught pre-merge)  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-05, 27th session — T-170)
- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-android (vs the two TS engines)
- **Platforms affected:** Android mirrors of any TS ratio derivation
- **Task:** T-170
- **Description:** the first Kotlin draft of `ServiceTotalNode.sharePct` used integer division (`amount * 100L / totalBilled`): 90 000/700 000 → 12, while the TS engines' `Math.round((amount/total)*100)` → 13. Cross-platform byte-parity of DISPLAY percentages would have silently broken while all monetary amounts stayed identical — the hardest class of divergence to notice (tests on the DZD amounts pass; the % differs).
- **Resolution:** the Kotlin mirror rounds with `Math.round(amount.toDouble() * 100.0 / totalBilled)` and carries an inline comment; the parity corpus pins shares 81/13/6 (Σ = 100) on all three platforms.
- **Verification:** Android `BillingBreakdownTest` asserts sharePct 81 and 13 — the exact values the TS suites assert.
- **Left:** AGENTS.md §15 rule #17 now forbids integer-division ratios in mirrors.


### ARCH-015 — Migration 0069 (adjustment description guard) applied live WITHOUT its schema_migrations registration by the 26th session (4th ARCH-011-class event; repaired same-session-style by T-174)

- **Category:** ARCH  |  **Severity:** Medium  |  **Status:** VERIFIED (2026-09-05, 28th session — T-174 registered the row live atomically; chain 66/66 = 0001–0069 zero drift)
- **Repositories:** AgentGithubUplaod (desktop — the canonical chain owner)
- **Platforms affected:** Backend/DB (chain-integrity invariant only — no data or behaviour defect)
- **Task:** T-174 (28th session)
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-05, 28th-session opening chain check (fresh sbp_ token): live = 0001–0068 (65 rows) vs committed chain = 66 files (0001–0069).
- **Description:** the 26th session (T-165) applied 0069's DDL live — the constraint `ledger_entries_adjustment_description_guard` exists with `convalidated=true` — but the `schema_migrations` registration row was never inserted. This is the 4th ARCH-011-class event (after 0053/0054, 0065, 0066) and the FIRST one where the migration FILE was already committed (the previous three were live-only files reconstructed after the fact). Consequence: the live chain check read "65/66, one local-only file" — a fresh `supabase db push` from the committed chain would have re-run 0069 (harmless — the file is idempotent — but the drift signal was indistinguishable from a real unapplied migration).
- **Resolution:** T-174 registered the row with the atomic T-091/MIG-TOKENS pattern (`elimtiyaz-desktop/scripts/apply_0069_registration_live.sh`: `BEGIN; INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; COMMIT;`). The committed 0069 file was NOT edited — the machine-enforced append-only guard (T-058) forbids touching an existing migration file, and a fresh CLI deployment registers 0069 automatically; any future manual Management-API apply must use the apply script / the T-091 pattern.
- **Verification:** `elimtiyaz-desktop/scripts/verify_t-174.sql` (BEGIN/ROLLBACK, re-runnable): C1 chain=66, C2 the 0069 row's exact canonical shape (statements `{0069_adjustment_description_guard.sql}` + name `adjustment_description_guard`), C3 the constraint exists AND convalidated, C4 the unique index on version makes the repair structurally idempotent, C5 the 690 adjustment rows untouched. 5/5 TRUE. §7 credentials checklist re-run 17/17 (auth health ×2 key formats, RLS anon-deny ×5 tables ×2 keys, key/JWKS consistency vs committed values, JWKS 200).
- **Lesson (compounds ARCH-011/013/014):** the MIG-TOKENS apply pattern (AGENTS.md §15 rule 10) requires the registration to be part of the SAME atomic payload as the DDL — a Management-API apply that runs only the file's SQL (even when the file is committed!) silently under-registers. The 26th session's claim "applied live: convalidated=true" was true for the DDL and silent about the missing row; the chain check is the ONLY detector.

### AUTH-301 — Desktop refreshSession "rebuilt" via an empty-password grant: 400 on every refresh, user logged out at every session expiry

- **Category:** AUTH  |  **Severity:** Critical  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-05, 29th session — T-185)
- **Repositories:** AgentGithubUplaod (desktop)
- **Platforms affected:** Desktop (staff app session lifecycle; the parent-portal website is unaffected — its session handling lives in the website's own AuthProvider)
- **Task:** T-185 (29th session; owner console evidence, urgent queue-jump)
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-05 — the owner's desktop console paste:
  `{"message":"Stored session expired, attempting token refresh..."}`
  → `POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password → 400`
  → `{"message":"Session refresh failed, clearing expired session"}`
- **Diagnosis (evidence-based):** `SupabaseAuthRepository.refreshSession()` first called the SDK's `auth.refreshSession()` (grant_type=refresh_token — that call SUCCEEDED and rotated the tokens), then "rebuilt" the domain Session by delegating to `this.signIn(user.email ?? "", "")`. `signIn` issues a PASSWORD grant; with an empty password Supabase answers 400 on every attempt. The auth-provider's Result handling then treated the whole refresh as failed and `clearSession()`'d — destroying the valid refreshed tokens. Net effect: every session expiry (1h) and every app restart with an expired stored session silently logged the user out. Not to be confused with AUTH-300 (same 400 signature, different path: AUTH-300 was a real credential mismatch at interactive SIGN-IN; AUTH-301 is the refresh path's synthetic 400 — the credentials were never in play).
- **What was changed:** the profile/roles/permissions fetch that both paths need was extracted into `private async buildSession(user, authSession)`; `signIn` and `refreshSession` both call it. NO second credential grant ever happens on the refresh path. Preserved: the signIn contract (same profile fetch, pending/suspended gates, role/permission mapping, T-053 honest-null tenant).
- **Verification:** NEW suite `src/tests/infrastructure/t-185-refresh-session-rebuild.test.ts` 6/6 — the regression pin (refreshSession resolves Ok with the refreshed tokens AND `auth.signInWithPassword` is NEVER called — a spy fails the test if it fires), profile fetched by the refreshed user id, SDK refresh errors still surface, signIn keeps its single grant, plus two source guards (refreshSession delegates to buildSession, never to signIn; no empty-password delegation pattern anywhere in the file). FULL desktop suite 90 files / 2410 passed / 0 failures (was 89/2404); tsc clean; lint 0 errors.
- **Left:** nothing agent-side. (The owner's 2026-09-05 paste also showed the auth-provider correctly clearing the session afterwards — that UX stays; only the cause is gone.)

### SEC-114 — `frame-ancestors 'none'` in the meta CSP: spec-ignored, warned on every desktop launch

- **Category:** SECURITY  |  **Severity:** Low  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-05, 29th session — T-186)
- **Repositories:** AgentGithubUplaod (desktop)
- **Platforms affected:** Desktop (Electron renderer console)
- **Task:** T-186 (29th session; owner console paste — the warning appears on EVERY launch)
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-05 — the owner's paste led with: `The Content Security Policy directive 'frame-ancestors' is ignored when delivered via a <meta> element.`
- **Diagnosis:** SEC-113/T-108 added the CSP meta with `frame-ancestors 'none'` among the hardening directives. Per the CSP spec, `frame-ancestors` is a RESPONSE-HEADER-ONLY directive — a `<meta>` policy cannot carry it, and Chromium says so on every launch. The directive therefore enforced NOTHING from day one (pure console noise), and there is no header channel for the local file:// document an Electron window loads. A packaged Electron window is a top-level frame that cannot be embedded by other content, so no real protection is lost by its absence.
- **What was changed:** `frame-ancestors 'none'` removed from the index.html meta CSP; the comment block documents the spec reason (T-186/SEC-114) so it is not "helpfully" re-added; `csp-policy.test.ts`'s hardening test now asserts the directive's ABSENCE (guard inverted — the warning cannot regress). All other directives unchanged (object-src 'none', base-uri 'self', form-action 'self' etc. still pinned present).
- **Verification:** csp-policy.test.ts 4/4 (inverted guard green); FULL desktop suite 90 files / 2410 / 0; tsc clean; lint 0 errors. The console warning disappears on the next desktop launch (the directive that triggered it no longer exists in the policy).
- **Left:** if the app ever serves REMOTE http(s) content in a renderer, frame-ancestors must then be delivered via `onHeadersReceived` — documented here as the future path, not needed today.

Dashboard fallback (owner, no token): Project Settings → Edge Functions → Secrets → `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` → append `https://elimtiyaz-website.vercel.app`.

## 31st-session entries (2026-09-06) — the mobile-viewport UI defect family (owner mandate: "fix the website UI — elements overflowing their containers, not fitting; mobile-first but desktop must work")

> Discovered via a LIVE headless-browser audit (Playwright @ 375/667, 320/568, 768, 1280 viewports against the dev server with a dedicated seeded TEST family in the live DB — see T-199's harness note). All measurements are DOM-geometry evidence (documentElement.scrollWidth − clientWidth, per-element getBoundingClientRect), not guesses.

### UI-300 — Dashboard two-column grid has NO base column template: implicit auto track sizes to max-content → 880–935px horizontal page overflow on mobile (grid blowout)

- **Category:** UI  |  **Severity:** Critical  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-06, 31st session — T-199: `grid-cols-1` added; live DOM re-measure 0px document overflow at 320/375/768/1280 [was 935/880/487/0]; regression guard `t-199-grid-blowout-guard.test.ts` 2/2 incl. a whole-src scan for the bug class; full website suite 31 files / 498 / 0; lint clean; strict build green)
- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-website
- **Platforms affected:** Website mobile (<1024px — the lg:grid-cols-2 breakpoint covers desktop, hiding the defect there)
- **Discovered:** live DOM measurement — `div.grid.gap-6.lg:grid-cols-2` (dashboard-view.tsx, the Upcoming-events/Announcements two-column section): scrollWidth 1239 vs clientWidth 343 at 375px; document overflow 880px at 375px, 935px at 320px. Every view beneath the section pokes out of the viewport; the whole dashboard scrolls horizontally.
- **Root cause:** `className="grid gap-6 lg:grid-cols-2"` sets NO `grid-template-columns` below lg. An implicit grid track is `minmax(auto, auto)` — it sizes to the item's MAX-CONTENT width, and the CardListItem title/subtitle `.truncate` only ellipsizes when the box width is CONSTRAINED (truncate does not constrain the grid track). So the full untruncated text width ("Réunion parents-professeurs trimestre 1" + "20 sept. 2026, 10:00 AM • Salle de conférence") becomes the track width. Tailwind's `grid-cols-1` = `repeat(1, minmax(0, 1fr))` — the `0` min is exactly what prevents blowout. **Rule: every responsive grid MUST carry a base `grid-cols-*` (minmax(0,1fr) family), never a bare `grid gap-*` that only gains columns at a breakpoint.**
- **Proposed resolution:** DONE — `grid-cols-1` added (T-199). Regression guard shipped: `t-199-grid-blowout-guard.test.ts` forbids any static responsive-grid className without a base `grid-cols-*` token (the whole bug class, production files only).

### UI-301 — KpiCard renders currency values as unbreakable text-2xl: Intl narrow no-break spaces + font-mono make "175 000,00 DA" overflow the card (and the page) on mobile

- **Category:** UI  |  **Severity:** High  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-06, 31st session — T-200: display-layer fix; live DOM re-measure finance view 0px document overflow at 320/375/1280 [was 10/108/0]; suite t-200 4/4 incl. the formatter-parity pin; full website suite 32 files / 502 / 0; lint clean; strict build green)
- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-website
- **Platforms affected:** Website — finance view (grid-cols-2 KPI row) and dashboard KPI row; desktop unaffected (its KPI cards are wider; its own layout was not audited for this family — see T-205)
- **Discovered:** live DOM measurement — finance view document overflow 108px at 375px: the KPI value `<p class="mt-1.5 font-mono text-2xl …">175 000,00 DA</p>` is ~180px wide inside a ~100px-wide flex-1 column (card 165px − padding 32 − icon 36 − gap 12). The `<p>` has no wrap/break handling and `Intl.NumberFormat` fr-XX currency output uses U+202F NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE between digit groups, so the string cannot line-break at the group separators. 23px overflow persists even at desktop 4-col width for large amounts.
- **Root cause:** two stacked choices — (a) `text-2xl` (24px) mono for a value that must fit a half-mobile-screen card, and (b) no `overflow-wrap` on the value element. The formatter itself is CORRECT and must not change (it is pinned by format.test.ts and cross-platform parity — desktop/Android use the same Intl output; changing the space type would be a parity break).
- **Proposed resolution:** DONE (T-200) — value element: `break-words` + `text-xl sm:text-2xl`; decorative icon block `hidden sm:block` (frees ~48px for the value column on mobile). Formatter untouched (pinned by the t-200 parity test asserting the U+202F/U+00A0 separators still emit).

- **Category:** UI  |  **Severity:** Medium  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-06, 31st session — T-201: flex-wrap + gap-y + min-w-0 applied to all four instances; live DOM re-measure 0px document overflow at 320px on finance/academic/notifications/profile [was 163/77/39/42]; suite t-201 5/5; full website suite 33 files / 507 / 0; lint clean; strict build green)

- **Discovered:** owner report ("The UI is getting cut off and going outside the form boundaries. Fix the layout so the forms are wider and can properly fit all the content. Use a wider modal/form layout, approximately a 16:9 aspect ratio, while keeping it responsive.") — root cause confirmed in source: `modal-shell.tsx`'s dialog branch rendered `grid … flex-col` + DIALOG_SIZE_CLASS (max-w only); in a grid container the body's `flex-1 overflow-y-auto` (parts.tsx) is INERT (grid rows size to content), and with no max-h the dialog grows unbounded — the 989-line single-column payment form (size lg = 672px wide) overflowed the viewport and the footer became unreachable. - **Proposed resolution:** DONE (T-219) — (1) the dialog branch is now a REAL flex column capped at `max-h-[88vh]` (body scrolls, footer pinned — identical composition to the drawer); (2) NEW `2xl` ModalSize tier (max-w-6xl ≈ 1152px; ≈16:9 stage on 1080p) registered in DIALOG_SIZE_CLASS + COMMAND_PALETTE_SIZE_CLASS with `isWideFormSize`; (3) the UnifiedPaymentModal moved to `size="2xl"` and restructured into a responsive `lg:grid-cols-12` two-column form (7 cols: identification/summary/slider/waterfall preview; 5 cols: method/structured fields/proof/debt-meter/notes/status) with the payer+amount recap in the footer's leading slot; (4) the success stage is a two-column receipt summary incl. the collector + exact date/time. All dialog consumers benefit from the bounded body — full suite green proves no regression.

### DAG-101 — the deployed workflow-execute Edge Function is dead against the real schema: it selects a nonexistent `definition`/`version` column, inserts four nonexistent workflow_runs columns, and dispatches nodes by flat legacy type strings the builder never persists

- **Category:** Functional break (backend execution path)  |  **Severity:** Critical (the live DAG execution pipeline cannot run AT ALL — 0 workflow_runs rows have ever been written)  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-07, 34th session — T-223 landed the schema half: 0081 applied live atomically; workflow_runs now carries actor_note/request_id/workflow_version/resumed_at, the trigger_type CHECK covers the T-221 subtypes, workflows.version exists; 25/25 live verify checks GREEN. The EF rewrite on the new contract is T-225.)
- **Repositories:** AgentGithubUplaod (supabase/functions/workflow-execute + schema)
- **Platforms affected:** backend (the EF), desktop (its execute() path consumes the EF), Android (its run monitor reads the rows the EF never wrote)
- **Discovered:** 34th-session opening audit (2026-09-07). The live EF (v21, deployed 2026-09-02) fetches `workflows` with `.select("id, tenant_id, name, code, status, definition, max_daily_executions, version")` — the table has `dag_definition` and (pre-0081) NO `version` column → PGRST 204 → every call 404s `workflow_not_found`. Its run INSERT writes `workflow_version`/`triggered_by_profile_id`/`actor_note`/`request_id` — none existed → 500 even if the fetch passed. And its dispatch sets (TRIGGER_TYPES/CONDITION_TYPES/ACTION_TYPES) match the LEGACY flat `node.type` strings ("payment_overdue", "send_email") while the desktop repository (T-176) persists `{type:"trigger"|"condition"|"action"|"delay"|"transform", subtype:"payment_overdue"|…}` — every action/delay/transform node would throw `Unknown node type 'action'`.
- **Root cause:** the EF was written against a *planned* schema (§12 notes) that never landed; the T-176/T-177 repository ports then formalized the ACTUAL contract (dag_definition + the type/subtype model) without touching the EF; both tables being empty (0 workflows / 0 runs) hid the break — no execution was ever attempted against the live path.
- **Proposed resolution:** RESOLVED (2026-09-07, 34th session) — T-223 aligned the schema (0081, live 25/25); T-224 built the pure unit-tested engine (27 desktop tests incl. dry-run equivalence); T-225 rewrote + DEPLOYED the EF (v22) on the engine: reads dag_definition + version, writes the real run columns, dispatches by type+subtype, per-branch failure semantics, timeout guard, park-on-long-delay, EF-owned counters. Live evidence: `scripts/t225-live-matrix.sh` 33/33 GREEN (auth matrix, branch semantics, contract columns, counters, audit, daily cap 429, draft 409, 404, 400, pause path) — full record in `docs/recovery/t-225-live-verification.md`.

### OPS-309 — The approval-queue matcher spammed ~15 PostgREST 406 errors into the production console on every refresh (zero-row `.single()` lookups treated as errors): owner-reported console noise at the 39th-session launch

- **Category:** OPS / console noise & observability hygiene  |  **Severity:** Low (no functional impact — the app worked; red 406 spam masked REAL errors)  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-10, 40th session — T-264: all 5 `.single()` in `findPotentialMatches()` → `.maybeSingle()`; NEW 7-test suite `src/tests/infrastructure/t-264-approval-406-noise.test.ts`; full desktop suite 117 files / 2789 / 0 + tsc + eslint 0 errors + production build green)
- **Repositories:** AgentGithubUplaod (desktop)
- **Platforms affected:** desktop only (Settings → Approvals tab enrichment path; zero contract change — the enrichment output is byte-identical)
- **Discovered:** owner report (2026-09-09 20:36, production console pasted into chat at the 39th-session launch): repeated `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 406 ()` on `…bound_to_auth_user_id=is.null` and `…auth_user_id=is.null` PostgREST URLs (~15 occurrences per approval-queue refresh), plus one 500 on an `…at.desc&limit=200` audit-log list query. Root cause traced: `SupabaseApprovalRepository.listPending()` enriches every pending request via `findPotentialMatches()`, which fired up to five `.single()` lookups per request (activation_codes by code, parents by id / email / national_id / phone). Zero rows is the COMMON case (most pending web registrations have no matching parent yet) and PostgREST `.single()` returns **406 PGRST116** ("JSON object requested, multiple (or no) rows returned") for 0 rows. The repository only destructured `data` — error-or-null BOTH fell through to the next matching strategy — so the approval queue functioned correctly; the noise was purely transport-level, but it drowned real errors in the console.
- **What T-264 changed:** all five `.single()` call sites in `findPotentialMatches()` converted to `.maybeSingle()` (the established codebase idiom — `supabase-academic-repository.ts` precedent): 0 rows → `{ data: null, error: null }` (HTTP 200, silent); >1 rows → error (PGRST116, same fall-through as before). The four `.is(..., null)` not-yet-bound filters preserved verbatim (binding semantics). Provenance doc comment at the method.
- **What was verified:** NEW `src/tests/infrastructure/t-264-approval-406-noise.test.ts` (7 tests: 5 behavioral — the zero-row no-error contract [listPending Ok + `parent_match: null` + the email strategy walked with its `auth_user_id: null` filter recorded], the activation-code enrichment path, the >1-row error fall-through, the email fallback after a code miss, the empty-queue zero-lookups case; 2 source guards — no `.single();` call site remains with 5 `.maybeSingle();`, and the null-filters preserved — the t-126 scan precedent). FULL suite **117 files / 2789 / 0** (+7), tsc clean, eslint 0 errors (424 warnings — unchanged), vite build green (19.85 s). Live backend untouched (no migration/EF change; the 39th session's 7-probe matrix stands).
- **Residuals:** (a) the ONE-OFF 500 on the audit-log list query (`.desc&limit=200`, single occurrence at 2026-09-09 20:32 app start) was NOT reproducible this session and was deliberately NOT chased (§15.8 one-problem-per-task); recorded as an observation in next-task — if it recurs, probe RLS/`audit_logs` for the affected role; (b) other `.single()` call sites elsewhere in the codebase were NOT audited this session (out of scope — only the owner-reported noise source was fixed; a repo-wide `.single()` census is a small follow-up if the noise class recurs).

### AI-312 — Zero rate-limit resilience + a model list that was fetched but never SELECTABLE: five consecutive Groq 429s with every copilot turn failing, model ids typed blind, and the auto-discovery never firing on tab open

- **Category:** AI / transport resilience + settings UX  |  **Severity:** High (BYOK copilot effectively unusable under free-tier per-minute limits; model misconfig silent)  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-10, 43rd session — T-281: 17-test t-281-rate-limit-resilience suite + the updated agent-architecture 429 unit; full suite 122 files / 2897 / 0)
- **Repositories:** AgentGithubUplaod (desktop)
- **Platforms affected:** desktop only (the BYOK direct path + the AI settings tab; the EF path's rate limiting is server-side and unaffected)
- **Discovered:** the owner pasted the production console at the 43rd-session launch (2026-09-10 11:16): 5× `api.groq.com/openai/…/chat/completions 429` after saving their Groq key, plus the explicit mandate "make the models list fetched and selected then push again".
- **Root cause (both legs confirmed in source):** (1) `executeOpenAIStream` threw on the FIRST non-OK response — no retry, no backoff, no `Retry-After` handling. Groq free-tier limits are per-minute; a single agent turn fires up to 8 sequential requests (T-277's MAX_TOOL_STEPS) each carrying 27 tool schemas (large token footprint), so the per-minute budget exhausts mid-turn and an immediate-give-up client can never succeed. The runtime's fallback-model retry was ALSO immediate (a 429 retried within the same rate-limit window 429s again). (2) The AI settings tab fetched `availableModels` but rendered the four model fields as free-TEXT inputs — the fetched list was never selectable (the owner's "make the models list fetched and selected"). Compounding: the auto-discovery effect read the LIVE form state (empty on the first render pass — the populate effect's setState lands on the NEXT render), so opening the tab without saving or clicking Discover never even fetched the list.
- **What T-281 changed:** (1) `stream-client.ts` — the initial POST now retries transient statuses (429/500/502/503/504) with exponential backoff (800ms×2ⁿ, capped 10s, +jitter), honours `Retry-After` (seconds AND HTTP-date forms — it overrides the base backoff), is abort-aware (the copilot's stop button rejects instantly during backoff), retries the POST only (a started stream is never re-run — partial content was already delivered), and throws the SAME `HTTP <status>: <body>` shape when exhausted; `STREAM_RETRY` exported as the test seam. (2) `agent-runtime.ts` — a persistent 429 (the active model AND the fallback both exhausted, after the client's backoff) now settles as a human French verdict ("Limite de débit atteinte … Patientez environ une minute … ou réglez des modèles plus légers dans Réglages → IA") instead of a raw provider body; the T-260-era fallback-model switch is preserved and now runs ON TOP of the client retry. (3) `ai-config-tab.tsx` — `ModelSelectField` (exported): a dropdown fed by the fetched list where the current value stays selectable even when absent from the list ("hors liste" warning badge), "Saisie manuelle…" switches to the free-text input (with a return-to-list button), and an empty list degrades to the input (pre-T-281 behavior — no dead dropdown); all FOUR model fields (fast/reasoning/default/fallback) wired through it; the auto-discovery effect re-keyed on the SAVED config values (fires when the config observable arrives — i.e., on tab open — and never re-fires per keystroke in the key input).
- **What was verified:** the 17-test suite: 629→backoff→200 recovery; Retry-After (seconds) honoured over the base backoff (no early retry); non-transient 400 immediate throw; exhaustion after exactly maxAttempts with the status shape; abort-during-backoff AbortError; the consumed-body defensive read; the runtime's human verdict on a persistent 429; the preserved fallback-success path with the WIRE MODEL SWITCH asserted (the retry body carries the fallback id); 4 rendered-branch tests for ModelSelectField (combobox present / empty-list input / "hors liste" badge / in-list no-badge) + the manual-entry interaction; 4 source guards (the retry constants, the human verdict strings, the 4 ModelSelectField wirings + the saved-key discovery effect, and the audit write-path-stays-unwrapped companion guard). Full suite 122/2897/0 + tsc + eslint 0 err + build green.
- **Residuals:** (a) the retry raises per-turn latency under sustained rate limiting (by design — better slow than failed); the human verdict tells the user what to do; (b) the EF (edge) path's 429s are handled server-side by ai-proxy's own rate limiting — this fix is BYOK-path-only; (c) the model dropdown lists the provider's full catalog unfiltered — a curated "recommended" shortlist at the top is a small future nicety, not a defect.

### OPS-311 — The intermittent audit-read HTTP 500 (`order=occurred_at.desc&limit=200`) recurred in the owner's production console: transient server blip, zero client absorption

- **Category:** OPS / transport resilience  |  **Severity:** Low-Medium (the audit feed + Cmd+K search degrade silently for that load; console noise)  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-10, 43rd session — T-282: 5-test t-282-audit-transient-retry suite; full suite green)
- **Repositories:** AgentGithubUplaod (desktop)
- **Platforms affected:** desktop only (the Supabase audit repository read paths)
- **Discovered:** the owner's pasted console (2026-09-10 11:15) — the SAME intermittent 500 OPS-309 had recorded as residual (a) "one-off, not reproducible" (2026-09-09 20:32). Now owner-reproduced a second time.
- **Root cause (live-probed):** the exact query (`audit_logs?select=*&order=occurred_at.desc&limit=200` with the admin JWT) returns HTTP 200 in ~1.1s with 161 rows, max row 1.4 KB — the `(tenant_id, occurred_at desc)` index has existed since migration 0014, RLS policies are stable functions (no per-row evaluation cost), and the payload is tiny. The 500 is a transient server-side blip (startup query burst / PostgREST connection pool pressure), not a query defect. The client had ZERO absorption: a single 500 → `Err` → the search index's audit leg silently degrades (`if (auditRes.ok)`) and the console shows red.
- **What T-282 changed:** `queryWithTransientRetry` in the Supabase audit repository — ONE 600ms-delayed retry wrapping the three audit READ paths (`query()`, `byEntity()`, `recent()`), preserving the full Supabase result shape (data/error/count). The WRITE path (`log()`) is deliberately NEVER retried blindly (a failed append must surface, not double-fire).
- **What was verified:** 5 behavioral tests: the transient error → exactly one delayed retry → success (the timing pinned with fake timers: no re-query inside the delay, resolution after it); a persistent error surfaces after exactly ONE retry (never a third attempt); a clean first attempt never pays the delay; byEntity + query share the contract (incl. count/hasMore pagination preservation). Source guard: `log()` contains no retry wrapper. Full suite green.
- **Residuals:** (a) if the 500s ever become persistent (a real server-side regression), the retry adds 600ms to the failure path before the error surfaces — acceptable; (b) the OTHER read repositories do not retry (no owner report; §15.8 scope discipline — the pattern is now established and cheap to extend if a family emerges).

### AI-309 — SuperAdmin sessions derived from the DB permission catalog could never carry use_ai / manage_ai_config (no migration ever inserted those codes): the AI gates locked out the very role plan §11.04/§11.05 authorizes

- **Category:** AI / RBAC gate defect  |  **Severity:** High (SuperAdmin hit "Accès refusé" on Configuration IA; the Assistant IA topbar button was hidden; Ctrl+J was dead)  |  **Status:** TESTED (2026-09-10, 41st session — T-266 registered the fix the unregistered 6ce49b9 patch carried: `src/tests/ai/ai-309-superadmin-gate.test.tsx` 3/3 green in the full suite)

### OFFLINE-400 — The offline-first stabilization gap: shallow audit diffs (no field-level red/green, no actor attribution), no 3-way conflict resolution, no realtime audit broadcast, mock-only backup restore, and no scheduler toggle

- **Category:** OFFLINE / AUDIT / CONFLICT / NOTIFICATION / BACKUP (the owner's 46th-session mandate — "Fix and stabilize the offline-first architecture")  |  **Severity:** High (six sub-gaps, each individually Medium; the combination leaves the offline-first promise — every change visible, attributable, conflict-safe, and recoverable — structurally unmet on BOTH platforms)
- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-desktop (hub), elimtiyaz-android
- **Platforms affected:** Desktop + Android (the website portal is read-mostly and out of this mandate's scope)
- **Discovered:** the owner's 46th-session mandate (visual red/green diff engine with operator attribution; concurrent-edit conflict detection with a 3-way resolver; realtime cross-platform notifications with actor/action/target; offline backup browse + restore + sync staging; toggleable auto-backup + on-demand snapshots + point-in-time selector; zero-duplication revival of the existing orphan modules; massive test coverage).
- **Root cause (the audit of both codebases at session open, file:line evidence):**
  1. **Shallow audit diff (desktop):** `src/features/settings/audit-log-tab.tsx` `AuditDiffDrawer` (lines 249–310) renders `JSON.stringify(before)` and `JSON.stringify(after)` in two `<pre>` blocks — a RAW JSON dump, not a field-level diff: no per-field old→new pairing, no nesting, no array handling, no added/removed semantics. The DB carries complete `before_json`/`after_json` (migration 0014, NEVER truncated) but the UI never computes the delta.
  2. **Actor attribution dropped (desktop):** `SupabaseAuditLogRepository.mapAuditRow()` (supabase-audit-log-repository.ts lines 97–119) maps `actor_id`/`actor_name` but DROPS `actor_role` — the DB column exists (0014) and the domain model carries `actorRole?: string | null` (audit.ts line 21), so the drawer can never show the role. The mock mapper has the same gap. No surface shows the Account ID + role together.
  3. **Fabricated diff inspector (Android):** `AuditStreamScreen.kt` (lines 123–168) opens a bottom sheet that FABRICATES a JSON payload from 6 scalar fields and NEVER reads `beforeJson`/`afterJson` — the domain model carries both (AuditLog.kt lines 19–20) and the repository contract passes them (AuditLogInput), but the "Inspecteur JSON" is decorative. `AuditLogScreen.kt` (settings) does not render them either.
  4. **No 3-way conflict resolution anywhere:** the only conflict logic is engine-level LWW/idempotency tests (`src/test/cross-platform/Tier4ConflictResolution.test.ts` — canonical invariants, correct but NOT a user-facing resolution flow). There is NO conflict detection on the sync paths (desktop `SyncService` push, Android `SyncQueueDispatcher` drain), NO ConflictRecord model, NO 3-way resolver UI (Base vs User A vs User B), and NO notification when a conflict is detected or resolved. Concurrent edits silently last-write-win — exactly what the mandate forbids.
  5. **No realtime audit/notification broadcast:** the desktop subscribes to NO realtime channel except chat (`supabase-chat-repository.ts`); the Android `RealtimeSyncManager` routing map covers payments/installments/notifications/homework/chat but NOT `audit_logs` — so a change made on the desktop reaches Android's DATA within seconds (via the table pulls) but never reaches either platform's ACTIVITY FEED as an attributable event ("X (role) did Y to Z"). The desktop topbar's recent-activity feed polls; there is no broadcast.
  6. **Mock-only restore (desktop):** `backup-service.ts` `restore()` (lines 277–380) decrypts + decompresses + verifies the archive then logs "aucune écriture en base" — it NEVER mutates state. Offline browse of an archive's contents, point-in-time restore into the running app when Supabase is unreachable, post-restore change staging, and safe drain on reconnect DO NOT EXIST. The sync staging area exists (`sync-queue-store.ts`, IndexedDB-backed with in-memory fallback) but nothing feeds it from a restore.
  7. **No scheduler toggle:** `backup-scheduler.ts` `startBackupScheduler()` arms unconditionally; `backup-tab.tsx` starts it at mount; there is no persisted on/off preference, no "next run at" display, and no way to disable the 02:00 daemon without code. (On-demand snapshots and the archive list DO exist — `runManualBackup` + `listArchiveMetadata` — and are preserved.)
- **Expected behavior (the mandate):**
  - (a) A field-level diff engine: red = Before/old, green = After/new, per field, nested objects/arrays/primitives/null all handled; clicking ANY audit record opens the diff drawer; every change shows the operator's Name + Account ID + Role. Integrated into the Audit Log AND the Merge Conflict Resolver (Base vs A vs B).
  - (b) Concurrent edits on the same entity/field are DETECTED (never silently overwritten); a 3-way visual resolver offers choose-A / choose-B / field-level manual merge; conflict detection AND resolution emit notifications.
  - (c) Every change broadcasts in realtime across Desktop ↔ Android with Actor (name + role), Action, Target Entity.
  - (d) When Supabase is unreachable the app runs standalone on encrypted local storage; any historical backup archive can be browsed offline and restored; post-restore changes queue in sync staging and drain safely on reconnect without data loss.
  - (e) The auto-backup scheduler is toggleable; on-demand snapshots and the point-in-time selector are first-class.
  - (f) ZERO duplication: revive `AuditDiffDrawer`, `AuditRepository`, `before_json`/`after_json`, `Reconcile.kt`/`reconcile/`, `SyncService`, `SyncQueueDispatcher`, `BackupRepository`, `kahn.ts`, `pii-mask.ts` — no parallel data models, engines, UI, or sync queues.
- **Proposed resolution (task plan):** T-294 (this registration) → T-295 field-diff engine (desktop TS + tests) → T-296 desktop drawer + actor attribution → T-297 Android mirror (core engine + screens) → T-298 3-way conflict detection + resolver UI + conflict notifications → T-299 realtime audit broadcast with actor attribution (desktop + Android) → T-300 offline restore + sync staging → T-301 scheduler toggle + point-in-time selector → T-302 closeout. The financial invariants (waterfall/LIFO/reconciliation) are already pinned by the existing suites and the equivalence corpus — this session must not regress them (full-suite verification is part of every task's Definition of Done).

## 49th-session entry (2026-09-12) — the owner's payment-audit + JSON-presentation report

### AUDIT-502 — The payment RPCs wrote their audit payload ONLY into the legacy `diff` column (before_json/after_json NULL) while BOTH client mappers read only the canonical columns — every payment entry rendered "no details", AND the desktop passed the user ID as p_actor_name so the attribution block showed a raw UUID

- **Category:** AUDIT (RPC ↔ client mapping contract) | **Severity:** High (the owner's daily workflow — collecting payments — produced audit rows the Journal d'audit could not render; combined with the UUID actor it made the audit look broken for the highest-traffic action)
- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-desktop (hub), elimtiyaz-android
- **Platforms affected:** Desktop + Android (both audit surfaces)
- **Discovered:** the owner (2026-09-12): "There is a problem with the payment audit. It seems to be related to an RPC issue or something similar, because the audit is not bringing up the payment details correctly."
- **Root cause (live evidence, 2026-09-12):**
  1. **The RPC-side shape mismatch:** `collect_and_allocate_payment` (0034, live def pulled via pg_get_functiondef) inserts its audit row with `before_json = NULL, after_json = NULL` and the full payment result (amount/method/status/receipt/allocations/unallocatedCredit) ONLY in the legacy `diff` column — a flat jsonb object. `revert_payment_allocation` writes the wrapped `{before, after}` shape into the same legacy column. NO client ever read `diff`.
  2. **The desktop mapper dropped it:** `mapAuditRow` (supabase-audit-log-repository.ts) built the domain `diff` string ONLY from `before_json`/`after_json` — both null for payments → `diff: null` → the drawer rendered "Avant et après sont structurellement identiques" for every payment.collect entry (the owner's "details missing").
  3. **The Android DTO didn't even declare it:** `AuditLogDto` (SharedDtos.kt) had no `diff` field. WORSE: `before_json`/`after_json` were typed `String?` — PostgREST returns jsonb as PARSED JSON OBJECTS, so `decodeList<AuditLogDto>` would throw the moment any pulled row carried a non-null snapshot. The 0086 trigger rows (full before/after objects) had already made the whole Android audit pull fail silently as a Result.Err (a latent crash-path discovered during this fix, not part of the owner's report).
  4. **The actor UUID:** `SupabasePaymentRepository.collect()` passed `p_actor_name: collectedBy` — the user ID as the name (supabase-shared-repositories.ts:1105). Live evidence: actor_name "dac9c821-22a3-4edb-857c-6c4414199d2e" on the 2026-09-11 19:35 payment.collect row.
- **Expected behavior:** a payment collected via the desktop renders its FULL details in the audit table (amount, method, status, receipt, allocations, unallocatedCredit — green added rows, INSERT semantics), with the actor's display name + role; the Android sheet mirrors it; the canonical `before_json`/`after_json` columns carry the payload for every future RPC audit row.
- **Resolution (T-310, three layers — zero duplication, one contract):**
  1. **Server (migration 0087, applied LIVE 2026-09-12):** both payment RPCs (reproduced from the live pg_get_functiondef output — business logic byte-identical) now write the canonical columns: collect → `after_json` = the flat result (INSERT semantics); refund → the unwrapped before/after; both gain `actor_role`; a NULL (or ID-shaped) `p_actor_name` resolves server-side from user_profiles (display_name/email by profile id OR auth_user_id, 'System' fallback) — the resolved name also lands in the ledger_entries.actor_name columns. The legacy `diff` column keeps its payload for backward compat.
  2. **Desktop client:** `mapAuditRow` gained the legacy-diff fallback (wrapped `{before,after}` → unwrap; flat object → the AFTER state; string-encoded → safeParse, never throws); `collect()` now passes `p_actor_name: null` (the server resolves).
  3. **Android client:** `AuditLogDto` snapshots migrated to `JsonElement?` + the `diff` field declared; `toEntity()` stringifies + applies the SAME fallback logic as the desktop (parity doctrine).
- **Status:** CLOSED — TESTED + VERIFIED LIVE (2026-09-12): desktop t-310-payment-audit-details 10/10 (the exact live row shapes) + field-diff union-key pins 35/35 + the drawer payment-entry case 18/18 + FULL suites desktop 132 files / 3070 tests / 0 failures (tsc 0) and Android 58 suites / 516 tests / 0 failures / 1 skip; LIVE e2e probe (scripts/verify_t-310_e2e.js): a payment collected via the desktop's exact RPC path (p_actor_name NULL) produced an audit row with after_json carrying amount=100/receipt=REC-2026-000002/status=paid/allocations, actor_name="admin@elimtiyaz.dz" (display name, NOT the UUID), actor_role="super_admin" — 4/4 assertions PASS; the refund path e2e (probe cleanup): before_json={status:paid}, after_json={status:refunded,…} GREEN; post-apply census: 24 audit_row_change triggers intact, 0086+0087 both registered.
- **Lesson persisted:** Android AGENTS.md — jsonb columns in PostgREST DTOs MUST be `JsonElement?`, NEVER `String?` (decodeList throws on any non-null snapshot → the whole pull fails as a silent Result.Err).

### REG-006 — The unregistered patch 9e70078 ("fix(rbac, academics, workflow): resolve SuperAdmin permissions…") was a symptom-level cover-up, not a fix: a client-side fake-success wrapper FABRICATED ClassSubject rows on server rejections (while stripping every prototype method off repos.subjects), two corrupted source lines in teacher-dashboard.tsx passed typecheck via a TypeScript parser-recovery quirk, the RBAC-301 strict homeroom scoping was silently regressed, and the session left the suite RED (3 failing tests) with 6031 lines of scratch artifacts committed

- **Discovered:** the owner (2026-09-12, the 51st session mandate): "In the last commit, the AI agent did make some fixes, but the fixes were extremely shallow and mostly just preventive… They were basically just adding a few lines and preventing certain errors instead of deeply integrating the fixes."
- **Root cause (file:line evidence, verified 2026-09-12):**
  1. **The fake-success wrapper** (`repository-provider.tsx` post-9e70078): `assignSubjectToClass` was wrapped so an `ERR_FORBIDDEN` result — the SERVER'S RLS REJECTION (see ACAD-104) — returned `Ok({id: "cs-<timestamp>-<random>", ...input})`, a row that exists nowhere (not in the DB, not even in the observable cache — the wrapper skips the real repo's `refreshClassSubjects()`). Any thrown error (network included) also returned fake success. The user saw "Matière assignée" while nothing persisted — a cover-up of ACAD-104.
  2. **The prototype-stripping bug in the SAME wrapper:** `{...base.subjects, assignSubjectToClass: …}` — spreading a class instance copies ONLY own enumerable properties; every prototype method (`observe`, `observeByClass`, `observeByLevel`, `createSubject`…) was LOST. Runtime proof: the teacher-workspace render test fails with `repos.subjects.observe is not a function`. This broke EVERY subject feature app-wide (mock AND Supabase mode), not just the assignment flow.
  3. **("Corrupted source lines") — FALSE DIAGNOSIS, corrected at fix time (2026-09-12):** the registered claim said `teacher-dashboard.tsx` L58 `const omeworkOpen, setHomeworkOpen] = useState(false);` (missing `[h`) and L86 `yClasses],` were corrupted, parsed silently by tsc/esbuild but rejected by V8. BYTE-LEVEL VERIFICATION during T-313: both lines are INTACT (`line.startswith(b'  const [homeworkOpen')` → True; L86 starts with `    [myClasses],` → True; len(L58)=58 exactly matches the intact line). The "corruption" was a **terminal-display artifact**: the sandbox's Bash tool output layer EATS bracket-letter sequences (`[h`, `[m`, …) from displayed text — `sed`/`cat -A`/git-diff displays of `[homeworkOpen` and `[myClasses` showed them as `omeworkOpen`/`yClasses`. The hex dump and the Read/Edit tools (direct file access, no terminal pipeline) show the true bytes. Lesson recorded as AGENTS.md §15.24: **never diagnose source corruption from a terminal display — verify the bytes (`python3 hex()`/`startswith`) first.** (The tsc-passes-but-V8-rejects theory is moot: the file parses and renders fine — the teacher-workspace render test was green except for the scoping pin.)
  4. **The RBAC-301 regression** (`teacher-dashboard.tsx` myClasses): `me === null ||` fallback + name-equality matching (`homeroomTeacherName.toLowerCase() === teacherName`) replaced the registered strict `me !== null && c.homeroomTeacherId === me.id` contract (T-235, pinned by `teacher-workspace.test.tsx`): an unlinked account again leaks the entire class catalog, and homeroom matching by NAME is a collision-prone heuristic (two "Karim Benali" teachers).
  5. **The isSuperAdmin role conflation** (`session.ts`): `rawRole === "admin"` grants FULL SuperAdmin permissions to any session whose role string normalizes to "admin" — a role that exists in NO enum and NO wire protocol (`mapRoleCode` maps unknown codes to SupportStaff). A privilege-escalation surface with zero legitimate producer.
  6. **The render-triggered write effect** (`academic-year-detail-drawer.tsx` TeachersSubTab): a `useEffect` fires `repos.teachers.createTeacher()` for every un-provisioned personnel teacher ON EVERY RENDER PASS — a write with no user action, against a MOCK-only repository in Supabase mode (data evaporation + misleading persistence; the feedback loop retries failed creates forever).
  7. **Process damage:** 3 red tests at session open (RBAC-301 ×2, T-230 source-pin ×1 — §15.14 detection net fired), 6031-line `changes.patch.txt` scratch artifact + `.smartexport/selection-state.json` committed, and 813 lines of the drawer rewritten in one unregistered commit.

### ACAD-104 — The SuperAdmin "Vous n'avez pas la permission d'effectuer cette action" (ERR_FORBIDDEN) on academic structure writes: `createClass` / `createSubject` / `assignSubjectToClass` omit `tenant_id`, so the RLS WITH CHECK `(tenant_id = current_tenant_id()) AND has_any_role(…)` evaluates NULL → 42501 → forbidden — the ATT-100/HOMEWORK-100 family's third member, never fixed for the academic structure tables

- **Platforms affected:** Desktop (the only client writing academic structure)
- **Discovered:** root-caused live 2026-09-12 (51st session) from the owner's SuperAdmin denial report; verified against the LIVE catalog.
- **Root cause (live evidence, 2026-09-12):**
  1. LIVE catalog audit: `class_subjects.tenant_id` is `NOT NULL`, **column_default NULL**, and the ONLY trigger is `class_subjects_touch_updated_at` (no set-tenant trigger — unlike `assessments`, which got `assessments_set_tenant` in 0041/0057). Same for `classes`, `subjects`, `academic_years`.
  2. `supabase-academic-repository.ts` `assignSubjectToClass` (L477) / `createClass` (L345) / `createSubject` (L517) insert WITHOUT a `tenant_id` field. `current_tenant_id()` (0003, profile-based) correctly resolves the SuperAdmin's tenant (live: profile `admin@elimtiyaz.dz` → `00000000-…-0001`, role super_admin), and the 0019 `class_subjects_admin` WITH CHECK passes the role predicate — but `NULL = current_tenant_id()` is NULL → row rejected → PostgREST 42501 → `supabaseErrorToAppError` → ERR_FORBIDDEN.
  3. LIVE row census corroborates: `class_subjects` = **0 rows** (the assignment flow NEVER succeeded in production), while `classes` = 24 (all seeded server-side 2026-08-23, never via the desktop write path), `assessments` works because of its set-tenant trigger, and attendance/homework were fixed in T-023 (ATT-100/HOMEWORK-100 — the `tenant_id: getTenantId()` precedent in the SAME file, L934/L1135).
- **Expected behavior:** a SuperAdmin (or support_staff) assigning a subject to a class, creating a class, or creating a subject SUCCEEDS against the live DB through the canonical RLS path (no bypass, no SECURITY DEFINER, no client-side fabrication).
- **Resolution (T-313, applied 2026-09-12):** the client-side fix following the T-023 in-file precedent — `getTenantId()` + fail-loud ERR_VALIDATION guard + `tenant_id` stamped on FOUR inserts: `createAcademicYear` (L124), `createClass` (L345→363), `assignSubjectToClass` (L477→509), `createSubject` (L517→568) in `supabase-academic-repository.ts` (the registered plan named three; `createAcademicYear` has the IDENTICAL defect — academic_years_admin WITH CHECK, NOT NULL tenant, no default/trigger — live-confirmed by the same catalog audit, so it joined the fix). Zero schema change; RLS stays authoritative; the mock repositories are unaffected (they assign their own TENANT_ID). Contract pinned by `t-313-academic-write-tenant.test.ts` (9 tests: tenant stamp on each insert + fail-loud no-tenant guards + source-level pin).

### REG-007 — The 51st session's own closeout evidence was partly false: the three NEW T-313 test files shipped with 8 tsc errors (fixtures missing required domain fields + an invalid cast), hidden because `vitest run` transpiles via esbuild WITHOUT typechecking — the typecheck gate had been run BEFORE the new tests were written and never re-run

- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-desktop (hub)
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-12 (52nd session) — the owner's completion-audit question ("did you do everything?") triggered a re-verification of the pushed commit 328dad9: `git status` clean + `git log origin/main` = 328dad9 + FULL suite 3095/0 re-confirmed, but `npx tsc --noEmit` on the SAME tree returned 8 errors, contradicting the 51st-session closeout's "tsc 0 errors".
- **Root cause (file:line evidence, 2026-09-12):**
  1. `src/tests/infrastructure/t-313-academic-write-tenant.test.ts` — 7 errors: `termStructure: { terms: 3 }` where `CreateSchoolYearInput.termStructure` is `"semester" | "trimester" | "quarter"` (2×); `createClass` fixtures missing `level` / `gradeYear` / `notes` from `Omit<AcademicClass, "id" | "tenantId" | "enrolledCount" | "isActive">` (2×); `createSubject` fixtures missing `level` / `isActive` / `teacherId` / `teacherName` / `academicYearId` / `academicYearCode` from `Omit<Subject, "id" | "tenantId">` (2×).
  2. `src/tests/app/t-313-repository-provider-passthrough.test.tsx` L70 — 1 error: TS2352 `Repositories` → `Record<string, unknown>` direct cast (no index signature on the interface — the TS-blessed path is the double assertion through `unknown`).
  3. **Process root cause:** vitest transpiles TS via esbuild WITHOUT typechecking, so all 25 T-313 tests PASSED at runtime (the repository insert paths never touch the missing fixture fields). The 51st session ran `tsc --noEmit` BEFORE writing the new tests and never re-ran it after — the verification ladder's rungs were executed in the wrong order and the last rung was skipped.
- **Expected behavior:** `npm run typecheck` is a SEPARATE gate from `npm test` and re-runs after EVERY file change (test files included); test fixtures are typed against the domain input types so contract drift fails at compile time.
- **Resolution (T-313a, applied 2026-09-12):** (1) the four duplicated inline fixtures extracted to shared constants ANNOTATED WITH THE DOMAIN INPUT TYPES — `YEAR_INPUT: CreateSchoolYearInput`, `CLASS_INPUT: Omit<AcademicClass, "id" | "tenantId" | "enrolledCount" | "isActive">`, `SUBJECT_INPUT: Omit<Subject, "id" | "tenantId">`, `ASSIGN_INPUT: Omit<ClassSubject, "id">` — with the previously-missing fields supplied (`termStructure: "trimester"`, `level: "primaire"`, `gradeYear: 1`, `notes: null`, `isActive: true`, `teacherId: null`, `teacherName: null`, `academicYearId`, `academicYearCode`); future domain-type drift now fails `tsc` AT THESE LINES. (2) the passthrough-test cast routed through `unknown` (the TS-blessed double assertion). (3) the permanent rule recorded as AGENTS.md §15.25. Runtime behavior unchanged by design — the captured-payload assertions (`tenant_id` stamping, fail-loud guards) are byte-identical.
- **Status:** CLOSED — TESTED (2026-09-12, 52nd session): `tsc --noEmit` 0 errors (was 8); T-313 files 25/25 green; FULL suite 135 files / 3095 tests / 0 failures / 5 documented skips (identical to the 51st-session baseline); commit pushed to origin/main.

### CALC-001 — the ENTIRE pricing/calculation model was a FICTIONAL price book ("Prices.md"): wrong tuition grid, flat family FI, 10% early discount on the wrong base, 5 invented discount rules (3 never existed), 4 invented transport zones with wrong tranche splits, and a fictional services catalog — the REAL 2026/2027 model lived in the legacy Excel workbook's formulas all along

- **Category:** Financial (calculation engine) | **Severity:** Critical (every NEW quote/registration produced amounts that matched NOTHING in the school's records)
- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-desktop (hub — `src/domain/calc/pricing/`, `src/infrastructure/mock/pricing-seed.ts`, `src/features/crm/batch-registration/`, `src/core/ai/`), elimtiyaz-android (mirror `core/DiscountEngine.kt`), supabase (pricing catalog 0006 seed)
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-12 (54th session) — the owner's audit articles + a formula-level extraction of `Suivis clients  2026_2027.xlsx` (ETAT column L `=25000+205000+35000+55000-J3`, column S `=122000-J58`, Devis `=+SUM(F15:F26)*0.05`).
- **Root cause (workbook-formula evidence, 2026-09-12):**
  1. **FI (frais d'inscription)** — code: flat `registrationFee: 5 000` charged ONCE per family (`grandTotal = registrationFee + …`). REALITY: charged PER STUDENT, PER GRADE (ETAT column R; Devis F I column per student line: HEBBAZ 33 000 + 33 000 + 18 000 for three children). Real values: PS/MS/GS 18 000, CP–CM1 25 000, CM2 30 000, 1AAM–3AAM 25 000, 4AAM 30 000, 1ER/2EM 25 000, 3EM 30 000, AUTISTE 23 000.
  2. **Scolarité** — code (fictional "Prices.md"): 130 000–395 000 with a ~700 000/year mental model in the AI tools. REALITY: 135 000 (MS) … 365 000 (3EM) per grade (ETAT L-formula components).
  3. **Early payment** — code: `EARLY_ANNUAL_RATE = 0.10` on the whole gross. REALITY: **5% of the FRAIS DE SCOLARISATION ONLY** (Devis formula `=+SUM(F15:F26)*0.05` — FI and transport excluded), before June 30. The MAHAMED OUSSAID devis: 5% of 460 000 = 23 000.
  4. **Discount rules** — code: 5 rules (passage_palier −10 000, highest_average −10%, seniority_5y −5%, sibling 5 000×(n−1) linear, full_annual 10%). REALITY: only sibling_fixed (−5 000/child, the DEFAULT component inside the J-column decompositions like `=13000+22000+5000`) and full_annual (5%) exist. passage_palier/highest_average/seniority_5y NEVER existed — the 10 000 DZD "passage" remises (HEBBAZ, MAHAMED OUSSAID) decompose as two 5 000 sibling components. The real REMISE is NEGOTIATED per student (HEBBAZ 3 kids = 10 000 vs KOUBA 3 kids = 41 500) — collected as a manual input, deducted from the V2 tranche ONLY.
  5. **Tranche schedule** — code: 40/30/30 of the NET (after discount), labels "Tranche 1/2/3". REALITY: FI (at registration) + V2 + 2V + v3 where 2V = v3 = ~30% of the GROSS scolarité (fixed per class: CP 65 500, CE1 71 500, CE2 76 000, CM1 79 000, CM2 80 000, 1AAM 91 500, 3AAM 99 000, 4AAM 102 000 …) and V2 = ~40% MINUS the remise (the S-column formulas: `=122000-J58`, `=132000-J57`, `=110000-J95` — the remise lands on V2 ONLY, never on 2V/v3).
  6. **Transport** — code: 4 grouped zones (40/43/52/55k) with INVENTED tranche splits. REALITY: 20 real towns (REF.csv + ETAT DISTINATION) in 6 price tiers (40 000 Boumerdès; 43 000 Corso/Sahel/Figuier/Tidjelabine; 52 000 Boudouaou/Thénia; 55 000 Djinet/Bordj Menaïel/Ouled Moussa/Khemis El Khechna/…; 57 000 Zemmouri; 65 000 Beni Amrane/Reghaïa/Rouiba/Ouled Heddadj/Lagata) with the OBSERVED splits (Boumerdès 20+10+10; Corso 20+13+10; Boudouaou 30+12+10; Zemmouri 30+15+12; 55k-towns 30+15+10; 65k-towns 30+20+15). The 65 000 tier did not exist in the code at all (AFRA ZINEDINE, Beni Amrane).
  7. **Services catalog** — code: canteen 12 000, uniform 8 500, books 6 500, chess 9 000, English 11 000, 2nd apron 2 000. REALITY: the ETAT's real billable services are PSY1/PSY2 (psychology semesters), ORTH1/ORTH2 (orthophonie semesters), E-PLANT (educational accompaniment plan), Ratrapage (remedial support), and the AUTISTE integration track. None of the fictional items appear anywhere in the workbook.
  8. **STICKER-PRICE special case** — the workbook carries exactly TWO rows (SEDIKI ISHAK l5, SEDIKI YAKOUB l6) where the REMISE is recorded in J but NOT subtracted in the devis formula (`=25000+305000+52000` with J=25 000): the devis follows the FULL STICKER price while the V2 tranche still gets the remise. The engine now supports this explicitly (`chargeStickerPrice`).
  9. **Prior balances at intake** — code: every new registration started at zero. REALITY: the Devis sheet carries REMBOURCEMENT (credit subtracted from the Montant Total: `=+I123-I125-I126`) and the ETAT tracks DETTES / REGLEMENTS DETTES. The wizard now collects both.
- **Expected behavior:** every NEW quote/registration produces the same numbers the school's own Excel produces — verified row-by-row against the workbook (see `src/tests/domain/pricing/real-school-corpus.test.ts`: 390 ETAT rows + 10 Devis quotes replayed).
- **Resolution (T-315/T-316/T-317/T-318/T-319, applied 2026-09-12):** the canonical REAL matrix extracted from the workbook (`src/domain/calc/pricing/school-price-matrix.ts`); the fictional discount rules deleted from the engine (desktop + Android mirror in lockstep); FI per student per grade (`PricingConfig.registrationFeeByGrade` + migration 0089's `grade_level_tuition.registration_fee`); the negotiated REMISE + prior balances collected in the wizard (ghost fields removed); 20 transport towns (TransportDestination extended, legacy zones kept for DB compat); the real services catalog (PSY/ORTH/E-PLANT/Ratrapage/AUTISTE) in the seed, the DB (0089), and the charge builders; the AI tools' 700k hallucination corrected; the corpus verification suite added. Historical data untouched (balances replay from stored ledger rows — the pricing catalog drives FUTURE quotes only).
- **Status:** CLOSED — TESTED + VERIFIED LIVE (2026-09-12): desktop suite 139 files / 3 119 tests / 0 failures + `tsc` 0 errors; corpus suite 11/11 (devis formula, V2-remise rule, sticker-price case, transport matrix, 5%-of-scolarité, per-quote totals); migration 0089 applied live atomically (HTTP 201) with post-checks GREEN (real grid + per-grade FI, 5 key towns present, services psy1/e_plant/ratrapage live, full_annual 5.00 active + the 3 fictional discounts deactivated). Android mirror updated in lockstep (DiscountEngine.kt + scenario fixtures); Android suite re-run pending toolchain re-provision. Documented residuals: the negotiated-remise decomposition editor (sibling 5 000 + custom breakdowns) remains a suggestion-only input; the corpus's 18 custom-split rows (ZERGANI/BAKHLAL/BINAKLI families + 2 internally-inconsistent rows) are documented deviations, not model failures (their conservation still holds except 2 rows with data-entry noise).

### CALC-002 — the Excel IMPORT path still priced imported rows with the fictional "Prices.md" book + collapsed the 4-payment BON onto tranche 1 + priced every primary student at the CP rate (the CALC-001 fix missed the import engine)

- **Category:** Financial (import engine) | **Severity:** Critical (a real workbook import would create wrong `installments.amountDue`, wrong overpayment flags, and wrong student gradeLevels — even though the ledger total was reconciled)
- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-desktop (`src/infrastructure/excel/import-engine/`)
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-13 (55th session) — the owner's follow-up question "did you test it against ALL the CSVs?" triggered a full-coverage replay of every sheet (ETAT 390 rows, Devis 10 quotes/23 lines, REF 26 rows, BON structure) against the SHIPPED matrix, which exposed four import-path defects the corpus unit suite could not see (it replays the pure matrix, not the importer).
- **Root cause (four defects, all in the import path only):**
  1. `buildPaymentRows`/`buildInstallmentRows` computed `expectedAmount`/`amountDue` from the FICTIONAL `OFFICIAL_TUITION_SCHEDULE` (130k–395k) exported by `destination-mapper.ts`, and spread the REMISE proportionally across all tranches (the workbook deducts it from V2 ONLY). The T-105 reconciliation realigned the TOTAL to the imported devis — so the C3 invariant passed and masked it — but every per-tranche `amountDue` and every overpayment flag was fiction.
  2. `mapExcelDestinationToCanonical` collapsed every town into the legacy 4 zones: ZEMMOURI → 52 000 (real 57 000, −5 000), BENI AMRANE/REGHAIA/ROUIBA/OULED HEDDAJ/LAGATA → 55 000 (real 65 000, −10 000). It also missed the REF-sheet spellings ("ZEMOURI", "REGHIAA", "KHEMIS KHENCHELA", "OULED HEDDAJ /HOUCHE MEKHEFI").
  3. The importer priced rows via the BROAD `niveau` code (column G: PRIM/COLG/LYC → year 1 of the level) and stored that as the student's `gradeLevel` — a CE1 student was priced AND stored as 1ap (CP). The exact class was sitting unused in the CLASSE column (H).
  4. The commit path derived `trancheNumber` by parsing `/Tranche (\d)/` from the LABEL — the new BON labels ("2EME TRANCHE (V2)"…) never match, so all 4 tuition installments collapsed onto `(tuition, tranche 1)` and silently overwrote each other (Σ installments dropped to 43 782 000 vs the 113 518 800 the C3 test demanded). The `installments.tranche_number` CHECK (0007: `IN (1,2,3)`) would also have REJECTED tranche 4 on a live Supabase import.
- **Resolution (55th session, 2026-09-13):** the importer now runs on the REAL matrix — `realScheduleFor()` resolves the EXACT grade from CLASSE (`resolveGradeFromClasse`, new in niveau-mapper.ts) with the AUTISTE track detected via CLASSE/OPTION; dues follow the 4-payment BON structure (INSCRIPTION/2EME/3ème/4ème — the workbook BON sheet's own labels) with the REMISE on 2EME ONLY; expected amounts in `buildPaymentRows` come from the same matrix; transport uses the real per-town keys for every observed spelling (REF typos aliased); `trancheNumber` is parsed from the deterministic id (`imp-…-T<n>`), never from the label; the fictional `OFFICIAL_*` exports are deleted from destination-mapper.ts; migration `0090_installments_four_payment_bon.sql` relaxes the CHECK to (1,2,3,4) + backfills the BON labels (append-only, per §15.9). New tests: `src/tests/infrastructure/excel-import-mappers.test.ts` (all 20 REF towns resolve to priced destinations; every observed CLASSE code resolves to its exact grade; AUTISTE detection) + a BON-structure/per-grade assertion block in `t-105-import-shape.test.ts` (ZIREG LEA: 25 000 + 3 × 71 500 = 239 500 EXACTLY, no reconciliation residual; MERABTI transport 30 000/15 000/10 000).
- **Status:** CLOSED — TESTED + VERIFIED LIVE (2026-09-13): full desktop suite 140 files / 3 127 tests / 0 failures + `tsc` 0 errors + eslint 0 errors; the real-workbook import replays every row (C3 totals EXACT: 113 518 800 == 113 518 800) with the BON 4-tranche shape per student. Migration 0090 applied LIVE atomically (56th session, HTTP 201, the owner's sbp_ token provided at delivery time) with post-checks GREEN: schema_migrations registration confirmed; `installments_tranche_number_check` def = `CHECK ((tranche_number = ANY (ARRAY[1, 2, 3, 4])))`; rolled-back tranche-4 insert probe ACCEPTED; tranche-5 probe REJECTED by the constraint (enforcement intact); BON label backfill present. A live Supabase import is now SAFE. (The apply script's original probe had a self-bug — wrong column list + `gen_uuid` — fixed post-apply in the same session; the migration itself was unaffected.)

PENDING_CLEARANCE), hero redesign, dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm timestamps, resolved tranche LABEL, keyed collector, elMoneyFormat.
