### GRADE-102 — Single-child parents never get an activeStudentId: every per-child view (grades / attendance / homework / finance) renders its EMPTY state forever — the owner's "grades are recorded in the system but the website is not displaying them" symptom

- **Category:** GRADE (portal per-child data routing)  |  **Severity:** Critical (the grades/attendance/homework of EVERY single-child family — the most common family shape — are invisible on the portal while the data is correct in the DB)
- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-website
- **Platforms affected:** Website
- **Task:** T-336 (docs/recovery/task-registry.md)
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-13 (60th session) — the owner's report ("Some exam grades have already been entered and recorded in the system, but the website is not displaying them correctly… make the website handle grades the same way as the desktop application") with LIVE evidence: the admin-entered assessments (3 rows, 2026-09-12) exist, the portal's PostgREST query returns them under the parent's RLS, and the Academic view renders them correctly for a bound parent with 2+ children — but reproduces "Aucune note pour cette période" for a bound parent with ONE child.
- **Root cause (live-reproduced):** every per-child view derives its active kid from the app store's `activeStudentId` (`useAppStore`), but that id was ONLY ever auto-selected inside the `StudentSwitcher` / `StudentSwitcherDropdown` components — which each view renders CONDITIONALLY (`{kids.length > 1 && <StudentSwitcherDropdown />}`; the dashboard imports `StudentSwitcher` but never renders it). A single-child parent therefore NEVER mounts any auto-selecting component: `activeStudentId` stays `null` forever, `activeKid` is `undefined`, `useGradesForStudent(undefined)` returns `enabled: false` → `grades.data` stays `undefined` → the empty state. The dashboard masks the bug with a LOCAL fallback (`kids.find(...) ?? kids[0]`) that never writes the store — so the child IS visible on the dashboard while grades/attendance/homework stay empty, which reads as "the website is not displaying the recorded grades". The same store-null also means a STALE persisted `activeStudentId` (e.g. after an account re-binding to a different family) silently empties every per-child view.
- **Location:** - `elimtiyaz-website/src/features/academic/academic-view.tsx:158` (`{kids.length > 1 && <StudentSwitcherDropdown />}` + `useGradesForStudent(activeKid?.id ?? null)` at L65) - `elimtiyaz-website/src/features/students/student-switcher.tsx:31-35,116-118` (the only auto-select effects, unreachable for 1-child parents) - `elimtiyaz-website/src/features/dashboard/dashboard-view.tsx:72-73` (the local `?? kids[0]` fallback that masks the bug) - same conditional pattern in `attendance-view.tsx:104`, `homework-view.tsx:55`, `financial-view.tsx:253`.
- **Evidence:** LIVE browser reproduction (60th session): a GoTrue test parent bound to the ATTOUCHE family (1 child, MASSIL, assessment 11/11/11 → 11.00 recorded by admin 2026-09-12) opened `#/academic` with a fresh localStorage → "MOYENNE —, MATIÈRE 0, Aucune note pour cette période" with NO student banner; the SAME session after the fix → full display (banner, MOYENNE 11.00, Arabe coef 3, 11.00 · 11.00 · 11.00). Data-path control: the exact PostgREST query of `useGradesForStudent` under the parent's RLS returned the row with the joined subject (11/11 checks, scripts/t-336-grades-e2e.py) — the retrieval layer was NEVER broken; only the id routing was.
- **Resolution (T-336):** the auto-selection moved to the AppShell — ONE canonical effect: when children exist and `activeStudentId` is null OR is not among the current children (stale re-binding), set it to `kids[0].id`. This fixes academic + attendance + homework + financial views at once for the 1-child case AND the stale-id case; the duplicated switcher effects were removed (one derivation, §9). Pinned by `src/test/t-336-active-student-autoselect.test.tsx` (8 tests: single/multi child, stale reset, valid untouched, empty unchanged + source scans).
- **Status:** CLOSED — VERIFIED LIVE (2026-09-13, 60th session): website 45 files / 599 tests / 0 failures (+14 T-336 tests) + `tsc --noEmit` 0 errors + `eslint` clean + strict `npm run build` green; live browser round-trip GREEN (before/after evidence above); zero-residue cleanup (assessments back to the 3 owner-entered rows, parent bindings back to the original 2).

### REALTIME-105 — the portal's realtime postgres_changes subscriptions target tables that are NOT in the `supabase_realtime` publication — zero events flow; freshness relies entirely on the T-033 fallback (window-focus + 5-min refetch)

- **Category:** REALTIME (publication membership)  |  **Severity:** Medium (the T-032/T-033 repairs remain the effective freshness layer; the subscriptions are dead weight, and "instant" updates advertised by the module docs do not happen)
- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-website (subscriptions), AgentGithubUplaod (the publication, migrations)
- **Platforms affected:** Website
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-13 (60th session, during the T-336 investigation) — a live probe (scripts/realtime-probe.mjs, run from the website repo with its supabase-js) subscribed to `assessments` changes (filtered to the target student) as the bound parent, wrote a row through the canonical `upsert_assessment_from_import` RPC, and received **0 events** in 8s (channel state "joined"); the CONTROL subscription on `audit_logs` (a `supabase_realtime` member since migration 0085) received **1 event** for its insert in the same run — proving the machinery works and publication membership is the gating factor.
- **Root cause:** Supabase WAL-based postgres_changes only delivers events for tables in the `supabase_realtime` publication. LIVE census: the publication contains ONLY `public.audit_logs` (+ the `messages_2026_*` partitions in `supabase_realtime_messages_publication`). The portal's five realtime hooks subscribe to `notifications`, `chat_messages` (×2), `installments`, `payments`, and `homework` — none of which are publication members — and any future grades subscription would hit the same wall for `assessments`.
- **Consequences:** - the T-032 realtime repairs (REALTIME-100..103) fixed the WIRING (keys, tables, filters) but the events still cannot arrive — the source-scan tests could not catch this; - the T-033 fallback (refetchOnWindowFocus + 5-min refetchInterval) is the ONLY effective freshness mechanism on the portal today (which, for grades, matches the desktop's own fetch-on-mount behavior — `SupabaseGradeRepository.observeForStudent` has no subscription either); - the notifications unread badge and chat updates arrive on focus/interval, not instantly.
- **Proposed resolution:** a hub-repo migration (next free number 0094) adding the six read-model tables to the publication following the 0085 pattern (idempotent membership guard; RLS already scopes delivered events per subscriber — verified for `assessments_select` parents/own-children) + a grades hook (`useGradesRealtime`) if instant grade updates are wanted. One migration covers all five existing hooks; no client change needed for them.
- **Status:** OPEN — T-337 (registered, not started; the probe script is re-runnable as the fix's RED control).

## 62nd-session entry (2026-09-14) — the owner's matière-architecture mandate (commit 158d806 "idk mattier is wrong")

### MATIERE-500 — the subject (matière) system fused IDENTITY with CONTEXT: one subject = one cycle + one coefficient (so "Arabe" only exists as a primaire matière), coefficients resolve through 14 divergent fallback chains across 3 storage places, and المراقبة المستمرة (contrôle continu) has no first-class representation anywhere

- **Category:** MATIERE (academic domain model) | **Severity:** Critical (the owner's own commit 158d806 patched 5 academic screens symptom-by-symptom — subject picker dead-ends, stale subjectId, empty catalogue fallbacks — while the underlying model cannot express a CEM Arabe course at all)
- **Repositories:** hub (desktop + canonical backend), elimtiyaz-website, elimtiyaz-android
- **Platforms affected:** ALL (desktop domain model + 14 UI surfaces, website academic-view + bulletin, Android Subject model with a per-component-coefficient concept that exists nowhere else)
- **Task:** T-343…T-349 (docs/recovery/task-registry.md)
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-14 (62nd session) — the owner's mandate: restructure the matière system at the root — canonical subject + context-specific subject configuration (per level, academic year, direction) with non-retroactive coefficients, add the missing continuous-assessment (المراقبة المستمرة / contrôle continu) concept into the GPA path, unify devoirs/exams/exam-sessions/reports/GPA on the 12-item canonical architecture, and sync the website to the same backend definitions.
- **Live evidence (census 2026-09-14, scripts/live_subject_census.sh — the Management-API SQL endpoint):** 12 subjects, each frozen to a single `cycle` with a single `default_coefficient` (AR=primaire/3, EN=cem/2, PHILO=lycee/2 — a 4AM Arabe teacher cannot find their matière at its CEM coefficient; the directory conflates "what the subject is" with "how it is configured in a context"); 3 `class_subjects` rows; 4 wide-row `assessments`; 0 `grades` rows (the 0004 normalized path is dead in production — the wide-row shape is the working truth).
- **Root cause:** three schema generations never reconciled: 0004 modeled subjects as per-class configuration carriers (normalized `grades` path, unused); 0029 re-modeled the subject directory with context columns (cycle, coefficient) ON the subject itself while denormalizing marks onto `assessments`; 0041 made the wide row canonical with snapshot columns — but no generation ever separated the subject's IDENTITY (code, names, domain) from its per-context CONFIGURATION (coefficient, identifier, passing grade, recipe, direction), so every platform invented its own resolution chain.
- **Anatomy (verified 2026-09-14):** (a) coefficient stored in `subjects.default_coefficient` + `class_subjects.coefficient` + `assessments.coefficient` snapshot, resolved by 14 different `a.coefficient || subject?.coefficient || 1` / `cs.coefficient || s?.coefficient || 1` chains (desktop: gpa.ts, grade-entry-screen, class-detail-page, class-grades-tab, class-subjects-tab, academic-year-detail-drawer, teachers-tab, academic-tab, operational-query-engine; website: portal-derive, bulletin.ts, academic-view); (b) the term-average formula is hardcoded (1,1,2) in the SQL trigger + desktop engine while Android carries per-component `coefficientDevoir1/2/Examen` on its Subject model — a divergent concept; (c) NO continuous-assessment component (المراقبة المستمرة) exists anywhere; (d) no direction (filière) dimension; (e) no exam-session entity; (f) `subjects.passing_grade` is global per subject, not per context.
- **Resolution (ADR-018, T-343):** the canonical architecture — `subjects` = identity only (legacy context columns become non-authoritative); NEW `subject_configurations` = context (subject × academic year × level × direction: coefficient, subject_code, passing_grade, is_extracurricular, grading_recipe with the `cc` weight); assessment rows snapshot the resolution at entry (coefficient + component weights, never retroactive); ONE canonical `resolveSubjectConfiguration` per platform replaces the 14 chains; NEW `exam_sessions` table; the formula generalizes to Σ(mark×weight)/Σ(weight) with the seeded default {1,1,2,0} bit-identical to the current engine.
- **Status:** CLOSED (TESTED + the live DB leg VERIFIED LIVE, 2026-09-14 — T-344..T-349): migration 0094 applied LIVE atomically (19/19 dry-run + 19/19 post-apply verify; the 4 production assessment rows byte-identical; the CREATE OR REPLACE overload trap caught BEFORE any live write); the desktop canonical module + resolver replacing all 14 fallback chains (T-345, ladder 146 files / 3218 / 0); the SubjectConfigurationsPanel (T-346, 147/3221/0); the website verbatim port + the cc mark end to end (T-347, 46 files / 607 / 0 + LIVE RLS probes: subject_configurations readable through the exact PostgREST path with the recipe JSON intact, the anonymous read blocked); the Android mirror (T-348, 62 files / 579 / 0 on the merged tree — SubjectConfig.kt + the cc-aware formula + Room 15→16 + the corpus runner ops); the cross-platform corpus 7/7 t345 subject_configuration scenarios EQUIVALENT through the real Kotlin mirror (the triple comparator: 319 scenarios / 317 equivalent / 2 pre-existing unrelated discrepancies). The architecture is now canonical on ALL THREE platforms + the database; the contrôle-continu (المراقبة المستمرة) component is first-class end to end.

### DASH-401 — topDebtors read synchronously from an async-seeded observable: first dashboard render shows "Aucun débiteur" / "Aucune relance nécessaire" / an empty Pareto while the DB holds 197 debtor families; the risk engine also receives only the top-10 slice

- **Category:** DATA (dashboard wiring) | **Severity:** Critical (the owner's screenshot set: the aging card says 58.6M DZD across 197 families while the Pareto card directly beneath says "Aucun débiteur" — a same-screen contradiction)
- **Repositories:** hub (desktop only — `src/features/dashboard/dashboard-page.tsx`)
- **Platforms affected:** Desktop (Dashboard Overview InsightsRail, Analytics "Flux Financiers" DebtorsParetoCard, SeeDetailsModal "Top débiteurs", and the whole `evaluateStudentRiskProfiles` debt leg)
- **Task:** T-351
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-14 (63rd session — the owner's dashboard-statistics investigation mandate), root-caused by code trace + live DB census.
- **Root cause:** `dashboard-page.tsx` line ~137 calls `repos.debt.observeSummary().get()` synchronously inside the year-range effect. `SupabaseDebtRepository.observeSummary()` seeds its `SubjectBehavior` cache ASYNCHRONOUSLY (`void this.seedSummary()` — a PostgREST round-trip), so `.get()` on the first pass returns the initial `[]`. The effect only re-runs on `yearRange` changes — by which time the cache has populated, which is exactly the observed "the list appears only after switching the year" behavior (owner screenshot 10). Additionally the page slices `topDebtors` to the top 10 BEFORE passing it to `AnalyticsTab`/`evaluateStudentRiskProfiles`, so even the populated state feeds the risk engine an incomplete debt dataset (families ranked 11+ evaluate as debt 0).
- **Live evidence (2026-09-14, Management-API SQL endpoint):** 197 distinct debtor families / 58,602,700 DZD outstanding in `installments`; the summary observable caches all of them; the first render shows none.
- **Resolution:** subscribe to `observeSummary()` reactively at the page level (the same `useEffect` + `useState` pattern the page already uses for the payments and installments streams — T-243/T-339), keep a top-10 slice for the display components, and pass the FULL sorted summary to the risk-profile engine.
- **Status:** CLOSED (TESTED, 2026-09-14 — T-351): the page subscribes `observeSummary()` reactively (the T-243 stream pattern); the full sorted stream feeds the risk engine, the top-10 display slice feeds the modal/rail. 8 regression tests incl. the after-mount emission race and the families-ranked-11+ contract.

### DASH-402 — the Analytics tab queries school-wide grades and attendance with EMPTY entity IDs (`observeForClass("")` / `observeByStudent("", …)`): both repositories build `.eq("class_id", "")` / `.eq("student_id", "")` filters that match ZERO rows, so GPA renders "—", attendance defaults to 100%, and the entire Diagnostic Actif / pivot / cross-risk / triple-risk surface shows all-zero

- **Category:** DATA (dashboard wiring) | **Severity:** Critical (the owner's screenshots 1–4: "Résultats : 0 élève(s) trouvé(s)", every class 0 DZD créances / "—" moyenne / 100% assiduité / 0 cas signalés across all 391 students)
- **Repositories:** hub (desktop — `src/features/dashboard/tabs/analytics-tab.tsx` + both repository layers)
- **Platforms affected:** Desktop (Analytics tab: ExecutiveDashboard triple-risk radar, OperationalQueryConsole, CrossRiskCard, PivotMatrixCard)
- **Task:** T-352
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-14 (63rd session). Verified in code: `SupabaseGradeRepository.observeForClass("")` builds `.eq("class_id", "")` (a UUID column compared to an empty string — matches nothing); `SupabaseAttendanceRepository.observeByStudent("", …)` the same. Mock parity: the mock filters `a.classId === ""` — also empty. Both modes agree, both are wrong for the school-wide use case.
- **Root cause:** the Analytics tab needed SCHOOL-WIDE streams, but the only contract methods available are per-student/per-class; the author passed `""` hoping it would act as a wildcard. There is no wildcard semantics — the repositories treat it as a literal filter.
- **Live evidence:** `assessments` live census = 4 wide rows (they would return for their real class_id); `attendance_records` live census = 3 rows. With `""` both queries return 0 rows; `calculateAttendanceRate([])` → 1.0; `computeOverallGpa([])` → null → every student "healthy".
- **Resolution:** add honest school-wide observation methods to the contracts (`GradeRepository.observeAll()`, `AttendanceRepository.observeAll()`) implemented in BOTH the Supabase and mock repositories (tenant-scoped, ordered), and consume them in the Analytics tab.
- **Status:** CLOSED (TESTED, 2026-09-14 — T-352): GradeRepository.observeAll + AttendanceRepository.observeAll added to BOTH contract modules (repository.ts + academic-repository.ts — the duplicated-contract reality documented) + the Supabase implementations (tenant-scoped, no empty-ID filters) + the mock implementations (store parity); the Analytics tab consumes them, the `""`-ID queries deleted. 11 tests: contract lockstep, query shapes, mock parity, tab source guards, the engine round-trip (observeAll data → non-null GPAs).

Semantic table documented: revenue = preset range; debt/waves/aging = academic-year window; call lists/Pareto/risk debt = point-in-time.

### DASH-407 — mock↔Supabase PARITY break in `revenueForRange`: the mock builds monthly buckets anchored to the RANGE (Sep→Août for an academic year) while the Supabase implementation builds them from the LAST 12 MONTHS FROM NOW — the same contract returns different month labels/drops out-of-window payments

The mock walks a cursor from `range.from` to `range.to` (academic-year-aligned labels); the Supabase version uses `buildMonthlyBuckets(new Date(), 12)` (NOW-anchored labels) then drops every payment outside those buckets even when it is inside the requested range.
- **Resolution:** the Supabase implementation mirrors the mock's range-anchored bucket walk (the mock is the reference convention — its labels match the academic-year window the page requested).

The parity test pins mock≡Supabase label conventions on the same fixture.

### UPLOAD-101 — the parent portal's document upload writes to a TENANT-LESS storage path (`{studentId}/…`): every parent document upload is RLS-rejected ("new row violates row-level security policy") — the `student_documents` table is EMPTY (0 rows) in production because the flow has never once succeeded

- **Category:** CROSS (storage path convention) | **Severity:** Critical (the portal's only parent-initiated document feature has never worked; the UI reports "Échec de l'envoi du fichier: new row violates row-level security policy")
- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-website (`src/features/profile/student-documents-card.tsx` — `UploadDocumentDialog.handleSubmit`)
- **Platforms affected:** Website (Profile view, StudentDocumentsCard)
- **Task:** T-360
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-14 (64th session — the owner's cross-platform upload mandate). Live RED proof: a parent JWT uploading to `student-documents/{studentId}/…` → HTTP 403 AccessDenied "new row violates row-level security policy"; the SAME JWT uploading to `student-documents/{tenantId}/{studentId}/…` → HTTP 200 (t-359-upload-e2e.py, checks E/F).
- **Root cause:** the dialog builds `objectPath = `${studentId}/${kind}-${Date.now()}.${ext}`` — folder[1] is the STUDENT id, but both parent storage policies (`student_documents_parent_write`, hub 0043) require `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = current_tenant_id()` AND `[2] ∈ own children`. The migration 0018/0043 path convention (`<tenant_id>/<entity_id>/<filename>`) was never followed by this call site (the file's own header comment cites "migration 0027" — a migration that does not exist in the canonical chain).
- **Resolution:** build the path as `${activeKid.tenant_id}/${studentId}/${kind}-${Date.now()}.${ext}` (StudentRow already carries tenant_id); correct the header comment to cite 0018/0043; pin with a regression test that source-scans the path construction.
- **Status:** CLOSED (TESTED, 2026-09-14 — T-360): the dialog builds the tenant-scoped path from `activeKid.tenant_id`; 5-test regression suite (t-360-upload-path-guard) incl. a whole-src guard on every production `.upload()` call site; website gates 47 files / 612 tests / 0 + lint + strict build + tsc 0. Live GREEN proof for the exact path format: t-359-upload-e2e.py check F (HTTP 200 under a bound parent's JWT). Commit 68ad0b6 (website repo).

### UPLOAD-102 — the desktop UnifiedPaymentModal hardcodes `tenantId: "mock"` in its payment-proof vault upload: in Supabase mode every proof upload is RLS-rejected, and because check/transfer methods REQUIRE a proof before submission, non-cash payment collection is BLOCKED at the source on the desktop

- **Platforms affected:** Desktop (Financials — UnifiedPaymentModal proof upload)

- **Root cause:** `uploadPrivateMedia({ bucket: "payment-proofs", entityId: effectiveParentId, tenantId: "mock", file })` — a mock-era literal that survived the Supabase wiring. The `payment_proofs_write` policy (0018) requires folder[1] = `current_tenant_id()`; `"mock"` never equals it. The two sibling call sites already do it right (`documents-tab.tsx` uses `student?.tenantId`, `homework-push-modal.tsx` uses `session.tenantId` with the T-053 no-tenant guard).
- **Resolution:** use `session.tenantId` with the SAME explicit French no-tenant failure the homework modal gained in T-053/TENANT-103 (global admin without a working tenant fails BEFORE the network call, never uploads to a wrong path); pin with a regression test asserting the literal `"mock"` never appears in the upload call.
- **Status:** CLOSED (TESTED, 2026-09-14 — T-361): the modal resolves `session.tenantId` into `workingTenantId` with the T-053 loud guard; the phantom `therapy-attachments` MediaBucket member removed (no such bucket anywhere); 5-test regression suite (t-361-payment-proof-tenant-guard) incl. the whole-src no-string-literal-tenant guard; desktop gates typecheck 0 / eslint 0 errors / 152 files / 3280 tests / 0 on the merged tree. Live GREEN proof for the exact path convention: t-359-upload-e2e.py check C. Commit 2fef316 (hub).

### UPLOAD-103 — the Android proof scanner uploads to a TENANT-LESS path AND the storage failure is silently swallowed: `LocalStorageRepository.uploadProof` pushes `{entityId}/{fileName}` (RLS-rejected every time), `NetworkTimeouts.guard` converts the RestException into `null`, and the UI reports success with a `file://` local path — the proof NEVER reaches the server while the user believes it did (the CROSS-200 anti-pattern reborn in the storage path)

- **Category:** SYNC (silent-failure class) + CROSS (storage path convention) | **Severity:** Critical (silent data loss: scanned payment proofs exist only on the device; the desktop can never see them; the screen even prints "Prêt pour la synchronisation Supabase Storage" under a local path)
- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-android (`infrastructure/local/LocalStorageRepository.kt` uploadProof, `domain/repository/StorageRepository.kt` contract, `ui/features/financials/ProofScannerViewModel.kt`)
- **Platforms affected:** Android (Financials — ProofScannerScreen; every future StorageRepository consumer)
- **Task:** T-362
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-14 (64th session). Live RED proof: a staff JWT uploading to `payment-proofs/{entityId}/{fileName}` → HTTP 403 AccessDenied (t-359-upload-e2e.py, check A). The repository's own KDoc already documents the INTENDED convention ("Path convention: `{tenantId}/{entityId}/{fileName}` (RLS-enforced)" — ProofScannerViewModel.kt) — the implementation never followed it (the §15.24 mirror-the-CODE trap, inverted: here the comment was right and the code wrong).
- **Root cause:** (1) the remote path omits the tenant folder; (2) `NetworkTimeouts.guard` catches ALL Throwables → a 403 RestException is indistinguishable from airplane mode → the code falls back to the local `file://` URI and returns `Result.Ok`; (3) `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 4s` — a 10 MB proof upload on a slow mobile network times out long before completion, deepening the false "offline" fallback.
- **Resolution:** extend the `StorageRepository.uploadProof` contract with the tenant parameter (mirroring the desktop `uploadPrivateMedia` params); upload to `{tenantId}/{entityId}/{fileName}`; REUSE `SyncErrorClassifier.isTransient` (existing implementation — §6) to separate transport failures (offline → local fallback, the sanctioned offline-first behaviour) from permanent 4xx rejections (RLS → `Result.Err` surfaced to the UI, never a fake success); a dedicated 60 s upload timeout.
- **Status:** CLOSED (TESTED, 2026-09-14 — T-362): the contract carries `tenantId` + `StorageBuckets.objectPath()`; the repository fails closed on a null tenant, wraps the remote leg in `withTimeout(UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 60 s)` and classifies failures with the canonical `SyncErrorClassifier` (transport → local fallback; 4xx → `Result.Err`); the scanner screen states the honest offline/remote status; 8-test suite (LocalStorageRepositoryT362Test); Android gates 60 files / 566 tests / 0 + lintDebug + assembleDebug green (toolchain re-provisioned). Live GREEN proof for the exact path convention: t-359-upload-e2e.py check C. Commit 5adc721 (android repo).

### IMPORT-106 — the owner's exact empty-restore scenario was NEVER proven: no test anywhere imported the real "Suivis clients" workbook into a COMPLETELY EMPTY desktop database and cross-checked every record, every field, every relationship, and every total against the workbook's own cells

- **Category:** TEST (verification gap) | **Severity:** High (the single most-asked question of the import pipeline — "if my desktop database is wiped, does the Excel import restore everything correctly?" — had NO evidence either way; the T-350 investigation proved the FIRST import money-exact on live, but the empty-state restore + re-import story was only reasoned about, never executed)
- **Repositories:** hub (desktop — `src/tests/integration/empty-state-excel-restore.test.ts` NEW)
- **Platforms affected:** Desktop (Excel import — mock mode AND the Supabase write path)
- **Task:** T-365
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-14 (65th session — the owner's "be 100% certain the Excel file from Suivis clients imports correctly and completely when the desktop database is completely empty" mandate).
- **Root cause:** the existing import suites used synthetic mini-workbooks with stub repositories; nothing exercised (a) a genuinely EMPTY store, (b) the REAL 619-row workbook, (c) a field-level cross-check against the workbook's own cells read independently via exceljs, (d) the FK graph, (e) the atomicity rollback from empty, (f) the re-import no-op.
- **Resolution:** a two-layer integration suite (see IMPORT-107/108/109 for the three real defects it caught before it could pass): Layer A — the ImportEngine + RepositoryStorageAdapter over fast in-memory stubs, per-row Excel cross-checks (charges/payments/balance per row vs the workbook's DEVIS/REMB/DETTES/REG/VERSES cells); Layer B — the REAL mock repository classes over a CLEARED shared store (the exact mock-mode desktop path). 13 tests. Pinned census anchors (a workbook replacement trips them loudly): 390 students / 253 parents / 891 payments / 1968 installments (1560 tuition + 408 transport) / 1283 ledger entries / payments Σ 55,227,100 DZD = the workbook's own TOTAL VERSEMENTS column / charges & installments-due Σ 113,518,800 DZD / the ZIREG LEA 4-tranche reference row (239,500 DZD) / 418 rows imported + 201 Devis/BON print-layout rows skipped + 0 rejected / a mid-import flush failure rolls the store back to EMPTY.
- **Status:** CLOSED (TESTED, 2026-09-14 — T-365): the suite (13 tests) GREEN end-to-end — every record restored, per-row financials exact vs the workbook's own cells, the FK graph intact (student→parent, payment/installment/ledger→student+parent), the aggregate totals reconciled, the canonical computeParentSummary statistics fed exactly, the auxiliary sheets classified (print layouts, not lost data), the atomic rollback to empty proven, and the re-import a complete no-op in BOTH layers.

### IMPORT-107 — re-importing the same workbook DOUBLED the entire financial history (mock) or SILENTLY DROPPED it (Supabase): the direct repository flush bypassed the migration-0027 identity contract — every ledger entry re-appended in the mock (every dashboard balance doubled), while on Supabase the `ledger_entries_source_uidx` unique index rejected every chunk and `bulkAppend` swallowed the error and reported success

- **Category:** DATA (re-import idempotency) + FINANCIAL (doubled balances / silently-missing financials) | **Severity:** Critical (the second import of the same file — the owner's exact recovery scenario, imported twice by accident or during a restore rehearsal — corrupted every financial total in one mode and silently lost data in the other)
- **Repositories:** hub (desktop — `src/infrastructure/excel/import-engine/storage/repository-adapter.ts` flushPendingBatches, `src/infrastructure/supabase/repositories/supabase-shared-repositories.ts` SupabaseLedgerRepository.bulkAppend + SupabasePaymentRepository.bulkCollect)
- **Platforms affected:** Desktop (both repository modes)
- **Task:** T-364
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-14 (65th session — caught by the IMPORT-106 suite while building it: the first Layer-A re-import assertion failed with the ledger at exactly double). The migration-0027 `upsert_ledger_entry_from_import` RPC path (the sync-queue) had ALWAYS been idempotent on (tenant, source_type, source_id) — the direct repository flush used by the desktop importer had simply never honoured the same contract.
- **Root cause:** (mock) `flushPendingBatches` called `bulkAppend(pendingLedgerEntries)` unconditionally — the old client-side dedup (`listExistingImportEntriesForParent`, removed in an earlier session as "no longer needed") was never replaced, so the pending batch was appended over the existing entries; (Supabase) the same unconditioned path hit `ledger_entries_source_uidx` → every chunk errored → `bulkAppend`'s `console.warn`-and-continue swallowed it → `Ok(entries)` with a phantom cache update (`[...entries, ...list]` — the UI doubled every ledger-derived total until refresh while the DB held nothing new); (payments) `SupabasePaymentRepository.bulkCollect` used a plain `insert` — a re-import with the same deterministic IMP-… receipt numbers hard-failed the whole batch on the (tenant_id, payment_number) unique constraint, blocking the re-import entirely.
- **Resolution:** THREE enforcement levels for the ledger: (1) the adapter pre-dedupes the pending batch against the CURRENT ledger stream by (sourceType|sourceId) — the mock path is now a no-op on re-import; (2) `SupabaseLedgerRepository.bulkAppend` writes via `upsert(..., { ignoreDuplicates: true })` (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING — the 0027 index is the identity arbiter), returns Err on any chunk failure (the atomic contract — the old swallow is gone), and updates the cache with ONLY the rows the `.select()` confirms as actually inserted; (3) `SupabasePaymentRepository.bulkCollect` writes payments via the same ignore-duplicates upsert on (tenant, payment_number) so already-imported receipts are skipped as a clean no-op. Installments already deduped by (parent, student, category, trancheNumber) — all three financial streams are re-import-safe. The adapter's flush also now honours a silent `Err` Result from bulkAppend (the T-012 atomicity fix applied to the direct path).
- **Status:** CLOSED (TESTED, 2026-09-14 — T-364): the t-364 suite (8 tests) pins the flush dedupe, the Err-propagation, the ON CONFLICT call shapes (upsert + ignoreDuplicates on both tables), the truthful-cache rule, and the mock↔Supabase parity; the IMPORT-106 suite's re-import assertions pin the end-to-end no-op (counts AND totals unchanged, both layers). The T-012/T-015 regression suites' fake clients were extended with the upsert surface (their fail-fast and receipt-allocation contracts re-verified GREEN — 11/11).

### IMPORT-108 — the mock payment repository had NO bulkCollect: every imported payment fell back to the generic `collect()` — which writes its OWN ledger entry (double-booking every imported payment beside the importer's canonical bulk_import entries), runs the waterfall allocator (adding amountPaid a SECOND time), and ignores the deterministic IMP- receipt (auto-generating REC-… so re-imports duplicate payments)

- **Category:** DATA (mock↔Supabase parity) + FINANCIAL (double-booked ledger, double-allocated installments) | **Severity:** Critical in mock mode (every dashboard financial total wrong after an Excel import on a fresh desktop install; re-import duplicated the payments table)
- **Repositories:** hub (desktop — `src/infrastructure/mock/repositories/financial-repository.ts` MockPaymentRepository)
- **Platforms affected:** Desktop (mock mode — the default first-run mode; the exact mode a fresh desktop install uses when restoring from Excel)
- **Task:** T-364
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-14 (65th session — the IMPORT-106 Layer-B store census failed: the ledger and installments did not reconcile until the fallback path was traced). The Supabase repository had carried the import-shaped `bulkCollect` since the T-012/T-015 fixes; the mock silently never implemented it, and the adapter's `typeof bulkCollect === "function"` guard routed every mock import through the WRONG financial write path.
- **Root cause:** the optional-contract method (`PaymentRepository.bulkCollect?`) made the mock's omission type-safe and invisible: the adapter fell back to per-row `collect()` (a UI-intent method: own ledger entry + waterfall allocation + auto receipt) instead of the import-shaped bulk insert the Supabase path performs.
- **Resolution:** `MockPaymentRepository.bulkCollect` now mirrors the Supabase contract exactly: inserts payments rows ONLY (no ledger entries — the importer's canonical bulk_import entries are written separately via bulkAppend; no waterfall — the installments already carry amountPaid from the workbook), honours the deterministic receiptNumber when present, and is idempotent by receiptNumber (existing rows returned as-is — the store's (tenant, payment_number) analogue). Globally-unique payment ids (the plain `pay-003` sequence collided after deletions).
- **Status:** CLOSED (TESTED, 2026-09-14 — T-364): the t-364 suite pins the contract (rows-only: ledger and installment counts UNCHANGED; deterministic receipts honoured verbatim; idempotent re-run returns the existing rows; the audit trail records payment.bulk_import); the IMPORT-106 Layer-B assertions pin the end-to-end store census (payments 891 / Σ 55,227,100 / installments amountPaid Σ = the payments total — impossible with the double-booking).

### IMPORT-109 — `findExistingStudent` matched the FIRST substring-search result by store order: a query for "LINA BELGRIMAT" ALSO matches a sibling named "MILINA BELGRIMAT" ("miLINA" contains "LINA") — re-import cross-wired the two siblings (MILINA renamed to LINA via updateStudent, a duplicate MILINA created, and each row's financial entries buffered against the WRONG student id)

- **Category:** DATA (identity resolution) | **Severity:** High (silent cross-wiring of related clients' financial records on every re-import — the exact "lost, duplicated, contradictory values" failure mode the owner's original investigation mandate named)
- **Repositories:** hub (desktop — `src/infrastructure/excel/import-engine/storage/repository-adapter.ts` findExistingStudent)
- **Platforms affected:** Desktop (both repository modes — the matching logic is adapter-level)
- **Task:** T-364
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-14 (65th session — the IMPORT-106 re-import assertion failed with a duplicate student; the BELGRIMAT sibling pair (rows 229/230 of the real workbook) was the live case). The repository search contract (`searchStudents`) is intentionally substring-based for UI search — the importer misused it as an identity resolver.
- **Root cause:** the adapter took `result.value.find((s) => s.parentId === parent.id)` — the FIRST result of a substring match within the parent's children, in store order. For the BELGRIMAT family both "LINA BELGRIMAT" and "MILINA BELGRIMAT" match the search query "LINA BELGRIMAT"; store order decided which row each workbook line updated — and the workbook's own row order (LINA row 229, MILINA row 230) made the WRONG sibling win the second row's match.
- **Resolution:** EXACT identity matching, order-independent: (1) parentId + displayName equality (the importer stores NOM verbatim in displayName — the canonical row identity); (2) fallback parentId + exact (firstName, lastName) equality. Substring containment is never trusted for identity.
- **Status:** CLOSED (TESTED, 2026-09-14 — T-364): the t-364 suite pins the BELGRIMAT pair specifically (LINA → stu-228, MILINA → stu-229, no duplicate created — the exact rows from the real workbook); the IMPORT-106 re-import assertions pin the no-op end-to-end (390 students before AND after, both layers).

### UPLOAD-104 — the portal's `student_documents` ROW INSERT omits `tenant_id` (the column has NO default): the storage upload now SUCCEEDS (UPLOAD-101 fix) but the follow-up table INSERT is RLS-rejected with HTTP 403 on every parent document upload — the row never lands and each attempt ORPHANS a storage object

- **Category:** CROSS (table-write tenant convention) + DATA (orphaned storage objects) | **Severity:** Critical (the parent document-upload feature is STILL dead end-to-end from the user's seat: the console shows `rest/v1/student_documents … 403` twice — once per attempt — after the 64th session had closed UPLOAD-101 as TESTED; the verification gap is the story)
- **Repositories:** elimtiyaz-website (`src/features/profile/student-documents-card.tsx` — `UploadDocumentDialog.handleSubmit` insert payload)
- **Platforms affected:** Website (Profile view, StudentDocumentsCard) — desktop never inserts `student_documents` rows (its documents-tab persists demo-shaped local records); Android uploads payment proofs only (tenant fail-closed since T-362)
- **Task:** T-367
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-14 (66th session — the owner pasted LIVE console evidence from the production portal: `rest/v1/student_documents 403` ×2 alongside the documented Firebase env warning). Live DB forensics (Management API SQL): `student_documents.tenant_id` is `NOT NULL` with **NO column default**; the `student_documents_parent_insert` WITH CHECK requires `tenant_id = current_tenant_id()`; the website's insert payload sends `student_id, kind, file_name, storage_path, mime_type, size_bytes, uploaded_by, description` — **no `tenant_id`**. NULL ≠ current_tenant_id() → SQLSTATE 42501 → PostgREST answers **HTTP 403** (the browser-console signature). The t-359-upload-e2e.py probe of the 64th session verified the STORAGE leg only (checks E/F/G/H/K) — the table-INSERT leg was never exercised, which is how UPLOAD-101 could close TESTED while the live flow still failed.
- **Root cause:** two halves never met: migration 0005 created the table with `tenant_id uuid not null` and no default (server-side writers were expected to carry it), migration 0043 added the parent INSERT policy keyed on `tenant_id = current_tenant_id()` — but the portal's insert payload (the ONLY production writer) was written against the pre-0043 world and never carried `tenant_id`. The sibling portal writer (`chat_messages` insert in `messages-view.tsx`) DOES carry `tenant_id: channel.tenant_id` — the codebase convention this call site missed. (Corroborating detail: `uploaded_by = current_user_profile_id()` is satisfied — the portal sends the `user_profiles.id`; the tenant is the single failing term.)
- **Resolution:** add `tenant_id: tenantId` to the insert payload (the dialog already receives the prop for the storage path since T-360 — one line, the `chat_messages` convention). Pin with a regression guard (t-367) asserting the insert payload carries `tenant_id` + a whole-src guard that EVERY `.from("student_documents").insert(` payload includes a tenant_id key. Extend `elimtiyaz-desktop/scripts/t-359-upload-e2e.py` with the TABLE leg so the e2e probe covers the full two-step flow: (L) insert WITHOUT tenant_id → 42501/403 (the RED proof), (M) insert WITH tenant_id → 201 + read-back under the parent JWT + zero-residue cleanup (the GREEN proof) — closing the verification gap that let UPLOAD-101 close early.
- **Status:** CLOSED (TESTED + the live leg RED→GREEN-proven, 2026-09-14 — T-367): the insert payload carries `tenant_id: tenantId` (commit 51ca7e5, website repo) + the t-367 regression guard (6 tests: payload term, uploaded_by term, storage-before-insert ordering, whole-src every-student_documents-insert-carries-tenant_id scan, chat_messages convention pin); website gates 48 files / 618 tests / 0 + tsc 0 + eslint clean + strict build green. LIVE E2E (t-359-upload-e2e.py, now carrying the TABLE leg): **L RED** = the pre-fix payload → HTTP 403 `{'code': '42501', 'message': 'new row violates row-level security policy for table "student_documents"'}` (the owner's exact console signature, reproduced); **M GREEN** = the fixed payload → HTTP 201; **M2** = parent read-back 200 with correct tenant_id + uploaded_by; **N** = cross-tenant tenant_id still 403 (the WITH CHECK is not weakened); **Z** = zero residue (docs count 0 before AND after — the production table is STILL empty: no parent upload has ever succeeded; the first real one will come from the owner's next portal session after their Vercel redeploy picks up 51ca7e5). Hub-side commits: eab7bfe (registration) + f829033 (the e2e TABLE leg). ADR not needed (no architectural decision — the client-payload convention `chat_messages` already established is now source-guarded).

### REPT-500 — Desktop PDF generation CRASHES on every realistic amount: `generatePaymentReceiptPdf`/`generateAccountStatementPdf` draw `formatDzdPlain` output raw — the fr-FR grouping separator U+202F is outside WinAnsi and pdf-lib's Helvetica `drawText` THROWS, so the receipt and account-statement PDFs (the two most-used documents in the app) never generate for any amount ≥ 1 000 DZD

- **Category:** REPORTING (PDF generation) + DRIFT (website fixed, desktop reference never did) | **Severity:** Critical (the receipt download in the financials receipts tab, the unified payment modal, and the CRM parent drawer all fail with "WinAnsi cannot encode (0x202f)" for every real tuition amount — the exact "every broken PDF generation" owner complaint)
- **Repositories:** hub (desktop — `src/infrastructure/receipt-pdf/payment-receipt.ts` [amountStr drawn 3×], `src/infrastructure/receipt-pdf/account-statement.ts` [formatDzdPlain drawn 6× + summary totals], `src/infrastructure/receipt-pdf/shared.ts` [drawKeyValue draws raw label/value]); the website port fixed the SAME bug in T-194/T-195 (`src/lib/pdf/shared.ts` sanitize-in-drawKeyValue + `formatDzd` replace `/\\u202f/g " "`) — the desktop canonical reference never received the back-port.
- **Platforms affected:** Desktop (Finance — receipts tab, unified payment modal; CRM — parent detail drawer; AI copilot — parent_statement artifact download)
- **Task:** T-368
- **Discovered:** 2026-09-14 (67th session — the owner's "all PDFs are broken, rewrite the reporting system" mandate; live RED proof via probe: `new Intl.NumberFormat("fr-FR").format(175000)` = `"175 000"` codepoints `31 37 35 202f 30 30 30`, and `font.widthOfTextAtSize`/`drawText` both throw `WinAnsi cannot encode " " (0x202f)`; Arabic-script names throw the same way — Algerian names are frequently Arabic-script).
- **Root cause:** `formatDzdPlain` (core/format/currency.ts) intentionally emits U+202F (the CLDR-42+ fr-FR grouping separator — pinned by the parity corpus, correct for HTML display); the desktop `drawKeyValue`/drawText paths draw the string raw; the 30th session's website port (T-194/T-195) added sanitization to ITS copy of `drawKeyValue` and its DZD formatter, but the fix never landed in the desktop reference — the exact DRIFT-011/§9 hand-copy divergence pattern, inverted direction.
- **Resolution:** sanitize at the DRAW layer of the desktop reference (the same seam the website fixed): `shared.ts drawKeyValue`/`drawFooter` + every raw `drawText` in payment-receipt/account-statement sanitize via the existing `sanitizePdfText`; amount strings through a WinAnsi-safe DZD formatter (U+202F → regular space before draw). Pinned by a RED→GREEN suite (t-368) that generates every document type with realistic ≥ 1000 DZD amounts and Arabic-script names.
- **Status:** CLOSED (TESTED, 2026-09-14 — T-368a): the t-368 suite (11 tests) RED→GREEN — the RED evidence captured the exact throw (`WinAnsi cannot encode " " (0x202f)` on every amount >= 1000 DZD + `(0x0628)` on Arabic names) at 9 failures; the GREEN run proves every document type renders realistic amounts and Arabic-script names. The fix landed at the SAME seam the website port fixed in T-194/T-195 (sanitize in drawKeyValue + a WinAnsi-safe dzdPdf amount formatter) — the desktop reference and the port now share the convention again. Commits 47fb21e (fix) + 827f8c8 (the REPT-503/504 legs that reuse it).

### REPT-505 — NEW DISCOVERY (67th session, found while building REPT-503): the legacy data-export Résumé sheet computed `outstanding = charged + adjusted − paid` against SIGNED ledger amounts — domain payment entries are NEGATIVE credits (entries.ts:118 `amount: -input.amount`), so the "Solde global en attente" was inflated by 2×|paid| on every export; the parents-sheet balance (signed sum) was correct, making the workbook internally inconsistent

- **Component:** backend — migration chain (`0003_rbac.sql`, `0019_rls_policies.sql`) vs the LIVE production database; NEW project `vebfehrpzajhstyhinnw`
- **Evidence (read-only pg_proc/pg_policies diff, OLD = source of truth):**
  1. `pg_proc.prosecdef`: LIVE `postgres`-owned `current_tenant_id`, `current_user_profile_id`, `has_role`, `has_any_role`, `has_permission` all have `secdef=true` **and** `proconfig = {search_path=public}`; the committed 0003 chain created all five **without** either. After 0099 the NEW project matches LIVE exactly (`MATCH_OLD: True`).
  2. `pg_policies`: LIVE `public.user_profiles :: user_profiles_select_own` predicate = `((auth_user_id = auth.uid()) OR (id = current_user_profile_id()) OR ((tenant_id = current_tenant_id()) AND has_any_role(ARRAY['super_admin','support_staff'])))`; the committed 0019 chain omitted the **leading `auth_user_id = auth.uid()` disjunct**. After 0099 the NEW predicate is byte-identical (`POLICY_MATCH: True`).
  3. `relforcerowsecurity=true` on `user_profiles`, `role_assignments`, `roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `tenants` on BOTH projects (FORCE RLS) — so only a `SECURITY DEFINER` function owned by `postgres` (`rolbypassrls=true`, confirmed on both) can evaluate those tables from inside a policy.
- **Root cause (why it happened):** the canonical chain was **hand-transcribed from memory/summaries** of the live database instead of dumped from it. Two transcription losses compounded into a fatal loop — (a) without `secdef`, a policy predicate calling `current_tenant_id()` executes as `authenticated`, so reading `tenants` (FORCE RLS) re-enters the `tenants` policy, which calls `current_tenant_id()` again…; (b) without the `auth_user_id = auth.uid()` disjunct, evaluating any policy on `user_profiles` called `current_user_profile_id()`, whose body is `select id from public.user_profiles where auth_user_id = auth.uid()` — re-entering the same policy. Both loops terminate only at Postgres's 2048 kB stack limit → `54001`. **All 83 policy-guarded tables inherited the failure through their predicates**, so the whole backend looked "locked" while every individual table was correctly created. This is the ARCH-005-class "structurally identical, behaviourally different" trap in its most expensive form.
- **Fix:** migration `0099_rls_helper_security_definer_parity.sql` (append-only; 0003/0019 are forensic evidence and untouched per §15.9): recreates the five helpers verbatim from the live definitions (`security definer` + `set search_path to 'public'`) and recreates `user_profiles_select_own` with the live predicate, fast-path disjunct first, plus `comment on function` documentation for each helper. Idempotent (`CREATE OR REPLACE` / `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS`). Applied via `supabase migration up --linked` to `vebfehrpzajhstyhinnw` ONLY; OLD project never linked in this session.
- **Verified:** `supabase migration list` NEW 0099 applied; `pg_proc` helpers `MATCH_OLD: True`; `user_profiles_select_own` `POLICY_MATCH: True`; **30/30 authenticated REST paths return 200** (the exact paths from the owner's failing console: `user_profiles`, `tenants`, `system_settings`, `academic_levels`, `academic_years`, `pricing_configs`, `roles`, `role_assignments`, `personnel`, `departments`, `classes`, `subjects`, `subject_configurations`, `class_subjects`, `students`, `parents`, `payments`, `installments`, `ledger_entries`, `expense_tickets`, `audit_logs`, `notifications`, `calendar_events`, `attendance_records`, `assessments`, `account_approval_requests`, `payments!parents(...)`, `personnel!children(...)`); anon still sees `[]` on all six protected probes (RLS intact — this RESTORED security behaviour, it did not weaken it).
- **Relation to AGENTS.md §15.4** ("Never weaken RLS, add `SECURITY DEFINER`…"): this is the **inverse** case and is sanctioned — §15.4 forbids adding `SECURITY DEFINER` *to make something work*. Here the `SECURITY DEFINER` attribute is part of the **production source of truth** and its absence is the defect; the fix restores exact parity with the live database and removes a denial-of-service (unbounded recursion) while leaving every policy predicate unchanged in strength.
- **Regression guards added:** (1) permanent rules 33–35 in `AGENTS.md` (never reconstruct a function/policy from prose — diff `pg_proc`/`pg_policies`; attribute-level attributes (`prosecdef`, `proconfig`, `relforcerowsecurity`, `rolbypassrls`, policy `qual`/`roles`/`cmd`) are structural; "N/N applied" is not functional parity; never widen a grant to match a permissive live default-ACL artefact; never diagnose a fresh clone from the client console — prove the server side first) — numbered 33–35, NOT 28–30, because §15 already contains rules 28/29/30 (see OPS-315); (2) reusable live verify script `elimtiyaz-desktop/scripts/verify_t-376.sql`, **12/12 PASS on the NEW project** (A: 5 helpers `secdep`+`search_path`+owner-`BYPASSRLS`; B: fast-path disjunct present + RLS still FORCEd on 4 tables; C: recursion probe resolved the profile, own-profile visible, tenant resolved, `super_admin` true, tenant-scoped read `academic_levels_visible=14`; D: unbound `sub` sees 0 profiles, `anon` sees 0 parents).
- **Dependencies:** none. Coordination: 0099 is the next free number after the concurrent T-371 (0097) and T-372 (0098) — no numbering conflict.

### OPS-315 — `AGENTS.md` §15 contains DUPLICATE and out-of-order rule numbers (24/25/26/28/29/30 each appear twice) — every `§15.N` citation in the docs is ambiguous (discovered 2026-09-15 during T-376)

- **Status:** OPEN (documented only; deliberately NOT rewritten this session — see "Why it was left open")
- **Severity:** Medium (documentation-integrity / instruction hazard, not runtime; but it silently corrupts the project's most-cited control: agent rules are addressed by number)
- **Component:** `AGENTS.md` §15 (lines ~305–326)
- **Evidence:** in document order `§15` reads `…23, 24, 25, 26, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 27, 25, 24, 25, 26`. Concretely: `24` = "diagnose source corruption from the terminal" (L305) **and** "mirror a doc comment — mirror the CODE" (L320); `25` = "RE-run the ladder after ANY file change" (L318) **and** "never emit timestamps from a Kotlin mirror with `Instant.toString()`" (L321); `26` = "never DELETE from `audit_logs`" (L306) **and** "never leave a vanity metric alive" (L322); `28` = "upload without the tenant path prefix" (L307) **and** "never reconstruct a function from prose" (L324); `29` = "locale-formatted money into a PDF" (L309) **and** my T-376 grant rule (L325); `30` = "file name collides with a directory index" (L311), "`§15.30b` zero-match DELETE semantics" (cited in T-372 docs, also at L311), and my T-376 console-diagnosis rule (L326).
- **Root cause (why it happened):** the block at L316–L322 (27, 25, 24, 25, 26) is a **merge artefact already present on `origin/main`** (verified: `git show origin/main:AGENTS.md` shows the identical out-of-order tail). Concurrent/rebased agents each appended their own rule with a locally-chosen next number and the merge kept both, so the counters diverged instead of being reconciled. New rules were then appended after `32` with numbers already taken.
- **Impact on this codebase specifically:** `§15.N` is a first-class citation format — `docs/recovery/change-log.md` cites `§15.25` (the ladder re-run), `§15.26` (audit append-only, twice), `§15.27` (RLS impersonation GRANT), `§15.28` (explicit probe `tenant_id`), `§15.30b`, `§15.32`; `docs/recovery/t-367/t-370/t-371-live-verification.md` cite `§15.26/27/28`. Because 24/25/26/28/29/30 each resolve to two different rules, **the same citation can now mean two different instructions** — a future agent following "§15.25" can land on either the ladder rule or the Kotlin timestamp rule.
- **Proposed resolution (deferred, needs owner/concurrent-agent coordination):** (a) renumber the orphan tail block (L316–L322) to continue after the highest existing number, or better, move each orphan next to its true siblings; (b) re-point every `§15.N` citation in `docs/` to the corrected number in the SAME commit; (c) add a guard (a `scripts/check-agents-rules-numbered.sh` style unit test, mirroring `scripts/check-migrations-append-only.sh`) that fails when §15 rule numbers are not strictly increasing and unique, so the counter can never drift again by merge.
- **Why it was left open (deliberate):** the user's standing instruction for this session is to minimise conflict with a **concurrently working agent**. `AGENTS.md` §15 is exactly the region the other agent appends to, and renumbering their lines (L316–L322) would guarantee a merge conflict on the very next push. My own three new rules were therefore numbered **33/34/35** (the first free numbers after the `32` block, appended at the end) instead of 28/29/30 — collision-free, and merge-safe. The renumbering + citation re-pointing is a single-purpose task for whoever owns the file next.
- **Dependencies:** none. Related: OPS-314 (whose rules were renumbered 28–30 → 33–35 because of this problem).

### RLS-500 — the CRM soft-delete was RLS-IMPOSSIBLE via plain PostgREST: `UPDATE parents/students SET deleted_at` fails 42501 "new row violates row-level security policy" for EVERY authenticated caller (super_admin included) because the staff SELECT policies (0019) carry `deleted_at IS NULL` and PostgreSQL folds the applicable SELECT-policy predicates into the UPDATE's effective WITH CHECK — dormant since 0019, exposed live by T-384's verification round (the T-381 student-removal surface was live-broken the whole time)

- **Status:** CLOSED VERIFIED (T-384, 2026-09-16 — migration 0100 [the canonical `soft_delete_parent`/`soft_delete_student` SECURITY DEFINER RPCs] applied to BOTH projects atomically with registration + the repositories rewired + the live harness RED→GREEN: the plain-UPDATE 42501 captured as the RED evidence, the RPC round-trip 17/17 + 17/17)
- **Severity:** High (T-381's shipped student-removal UI was a live no-op-with-error — every Supprimer click would toast "Une erreur inattendue s'est produite"; the parent removal would have shipped the same; the Excel import rollback path (deleteParent) was equally broken; NONE of it was caught by the suites because the repository tests mock the client — a suite-green repository method is not a working method)
- **Component:** parents + students RLS policy sets (0019/0043/0046); the desktop Supabase repositories; migration 0100
- **Evidence (the full bisection, live on production, 74th session):** (1) the REST bisect — PATCH {address}/{is_active}/{first_name}/{updated_at} all 204 OK, PATCH {deleted_at} 403 42501; (2) `return=representation` confirmed the "OK" PATCHes genuinely land (the row changes), so the failure is deleted_at-specific; (3) the SQL impersonation repro (`SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated` + the admin claims — the AUTH id as sub, NOT user_profiles.id which differs): same 42501 in pure SQL — not a PostgREST artefact; (4) the policy-drop bisection in transactions: with ONLY `parents_update` the UPDATE passes; add `parents_select` back → 42501 (same for students); (5) EXPLAIN shows the UPDATE's Filter folding the SELECT-policy predicates (`deleted_at IS NULL AND tenant = … AND (staff-roles OR parent-self) AND (select-policies…)`); (6) the students baseline: the same 42501. Root mechanism: for UPDATE, PostgreSQL applies the applicable SELECT policies (visibility) and their predicates on the result state — the NEW row with `deleted_at` set can never satisfy `deleted_at IS NULL`, so the effective WITH CHECK fails for every role.
- **Root cause:** 0019's staff SELECT policies filter `deleted_at IS NULL` (correct — soft-deleted rows must vanish from staff lists), and no writer ever SET deleted_at via PostgREST until T-381/T-384 surfaced the removal buttons — the constraint was never hit, never tested live, and invisible to client-mocked suites.
- **What was changed (T-384):** migration 0100 — `public.soft_delete_parent(p_parent_id)` + `public.soft_delete_student(p_student_id)`: SECURITY DEFINER + `search_path = public`, super_admin gate (the *_delete RLS mirror + the EF precedent), explicit tenant scope (not_found for unknown/already-deleted/cross-tenant — §15.30b), the active-students guard for parents (counts NON-deleted students only → `active_students_exist` with the count), race-safe UPDATE (re-checks deleted_at), `write_audit_log` parent.delete/student.delete intent entries (the 0086 trigger keeps writing its mechanism entry — both honest); the desktop repositories rewired — `deleteParent`/`deleteStudent` call the RPCs and map the envelopes; the t-384 suite pins the wiring + the NO-plain-deleted_at-UPDATE source guard; the t-384 E2E harness captures the RED evidence (D1/D2) + the full RPC round-trip.
- **Deliberately NOT changed:** the SELECT policies (removing `deleted_at IS NULL` would resurrect soft-deleted rows in every staff list — the catastrophic non-fix); the 0086 audit trigger; the hard-delete RLS policies (parents_delete/students_delete remain super_admin-only, unused by the desktop — the soft-delete preserves financial history per the STUDENT-500 precedent).
- **Registered residual (documented):** the RPC role gate is super_admin-only while the desktop UI permissions (DeleteParent/DeleteStudent) are RBAC-matrix-grantable — if the owner grants either permission to a non-super_admin role, the RPC gate must be widened in the same change (a one-line policy decision, not silently).
- **Dependencies:** none. Related: PARENT-500 (the task that exposed it), STUDENT-500 (the live-broken T-381 surface this fixed), §15.36 (the AGENTS.md rule this became), §15.30b (the zero-match honesty — the debugging traps it caused), §15.27 (the claims-impersonation convention — the sub-must-be-the-AUTH-id correction).

### SYNC-300 — the desktop sync push sent BLANK STRINGS into typed RPC parameters: `p_class_id: ""` (the `??` coalescing operator converts only null/undefined, NEVER "") reached `upsert_student_from_import`'s `uuid` parameter and PostgREST answered the reported HTTP 400 `22P02 invalid input syntax for type uuid: ""` BEFORE the SECURITY DEFINER body could run — and the same defect class sat on every date/timestamp-typed argument in the dispatcher

- **Status:** CLOSED VERIFIED (T-387, 2026-09-17 — registered BEFORE the fix per §13, fixed same-session: `blankToNull()` for every date/timestamptz param + `uuidOrNull()` (the exported `isUuid` guard) for every optional uuid param in default-push-handler.ts; the t-387 suite 14/14; verify_t-387.sql 7/7 live; the t-387-rpc-blank-args-e2e.py 14/14 on NEW + 13/14 on OLD [the one FAIL is the OPS-316 discovery, not SYNC-300]; evidence: docs/recovery/t-387-live-verification.md)
- **Severity:** Medium (every affected queue entry is marked `failed` with a cryptic cast error and re-tried forever with backoff — the import data never lands; the error body names neither the field nor the entity, so the operator cannot self-serve)
- **Component:** desktop sync push dispatcher (`src/infrastructure/sync/default-push-handler.ts`) — the student/attendance/grade/payment/ledger/installment upsert RPC calls
- **Evidence (live, both projects, 2026-09-17):** the exact desktop payload shape with `p_class_id: ""` → HTTP 400 `{"code":"22P02","message":"invalid input syntax for type uuid: \"\""}`; the identical call with `p_class_id: null` → HTTP 200 + `out_student_id`; `p_date_of_birth: ""` → HTTP 400 (the 22007 sibling — dates share the class). The reported student-import 400 was initially attributed to missing 0023 seed data — DISPROVEN live: both projects carry the full canonical census (tenants=1, roles=11, permissions=56, default tenant present, super_admin=56/56) and the RPC succeeds on valid args.
- **Root cause:** `??` is a nullish operator — an empty string is NOT nullish, so `(p.classId as string) ?? … ?? null` passes `""` through. PostgREST casts JSON arguments to the function's declared parameter types at the gateway; `""::uuid` (22P02) and `""::date` (22007) fail before the RPC body's `NULLIF(TRIM(…),'')` normalization can run. READ-path sibling already known: ACAD-501 (`?class_id=eq.` filters, fixed T-373) — this is the WRITE-path member of the same family.
- **What was changed (T-387):** `blankToNull()` (blank/whitespace → null) applied to `p_date_of_birth`, `p_collected_at`, `p_at`, `p_due_date`, `p_paid_date`, `p_record_date`; `uuidOrNull()` (reuse of the exported `isUuid`, the line-1268 convention) applied to `p_class_id` ×3 (student/attendance/grade), `p_collected_by`, `p_recorded_by`, `p_entered_by`. ONLY `DEFAULT NULL` (optional) params are guarded — required uuid params (`p_student_id`, `p_subject_id`) deliberately stay loud (a blank there is a data error that must fail with the RPC's own validation). `types.ts` re-aligned to the live `pg_proc` signature (`upsert_student_from_import` + the 0028 params `p_grade_level_code`/`p_transport_tier`/`p_payment_plan` + the 0031 `out_*` Returns). AGENTS.md §15.37 added (the rule).
- **Deliberately NOT changed:** the RPC server-side signatures/behavior (the canonical chain owns them — 0027/0031/0037/0041); `supabase-shared-repositories.ts` `createStudent`'s `p_class_id: input.classId ?? null` (its import path passes `classId: null` explicitly — repository-adapter line 807; noted as a same-class surface if a UI caller ever sends `""`); the mock-mode behaviour; the homework direct upsert (no typed RPC params).
- **Dependencies:** none. Related: ACAD-501 (the read-path sibling), T-022 (the dispatcher's original correctness suite — still green post-fix), T-386 (the session's second discovery, OPS-316).

### OPS-316 — production migration-history registration drift: `0099_rls_helper_security_definer_parity.sql` is committed in the chain and LIVE-functionally present on production `hkvkefubghbbotgnteir` (12/12 verify_t-376 PASS), but its `schema_migrations` row was never inserted there — T-376 applied 0099 to the NEW project only (production was deliberately read-only that session), so production reports 96/97 applied and every future `supabase migration list` / `db push` diff flags a migration whose DDL is already in place

- **Status:** CLOSED VERIFIED (T-386, 2026-09-17 — the atomic heal ran against production hkvkefubghbbotgnteir: apply_0099_live.sh → HTTP 201, the registration INSERT [the 0100-in-file pattern: version+statements+name] + the idempotent 0099 DDL in ONE transaction; post-heal evidence: migrations_applied 96→97, verify_t-376.sql on OLD 12/12 [the helpers' shape untouched], verify_t-387.sql on OLD 7/7 [C3 parity = 97], t-387-rpc-blank-args-e2e.py on OLD 14/14 [was 13/14 — G3 green])

- **Component:** production `hkvkefubghbbotgnteir` `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`
- **Evidence (live, 2026-09-17):** the t-387 E2E G3 check on OLD → `applied=96`; the version-by-version diff vs the local chain → exactly `{'0099'}` missing; `verify_t-376.sql` against OLD → 12/12 PASS (A1 5/5 secdef helpers, A2 5/5 search_path, B1 fast-path qual, C1 no recursion, C4 super_admin…); the T-376 task entry Scope line: "NEW project ONLY. OLD project read-only".

The §15.10 rule ("file + registration in the SAME change") was satisfied for the chain/NEW but not for production's history row.
- **What was changed (T-386, applied):** `elimtiyaz-desktop/scripts/apply_0099_live.sh` (the apply_0100_live.sh pattern — atomic single-call apply + registration, targeting OLD only since NEW already carries both; the INSERT follows the 0100-in-file column pattern [version, statements, name] with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING so re-runs are no-ops) + the post-verify legs all green (see the status line).

### I18N-501 — the DESKTOP's 3-locale coverage is INCOMPLETE: 3,643 hardcoded user-visible strings across 174 UI files (2,924 unique, ~1,176 of them English-source — the "English text" the owner sees), NO English locale at all (supportedLngs = [fr, ar] only), an Arabic dictionary that is a declared SUBSET (~290 lines vs the 119 `t()` calls in use), and an Arabic webfont that fails offline (Google-Fonts CDN in an Electron app) — the desktop half of the owner's 3-language mandate, discovered by the owner's review (2026-09-17: "Are you sure you translated the entire desktop? I can still see a lot of English text, and in the Arabic version, many things are still not translated. Also, fix the Arabic font and choose a better one that looks clean and professional.")

- **Status:** OPEN (registered BEFORE the fix per §13, 77th session 2026-09-17)
- **Severity:** High (the owner's explicit review finding: the T-385 portal pass covered the WEBSITE repo only; the desktop — the staff's primary daily tool — ships `lng: "fr"`, `supportedLngs: ["fr", "ar"]`, no `en` resource, and only 18 of 220 non-test components call `useTranslation` (~8%); every other screen renders its authoring-language literals: French for most chrome, ENGLISH for large surfaces — the analytics console, executive cards, payroll, settings tabs — so the owner sees English regardless of locale, and switching to Arabic leaves ~92% of the UI untranslated)
- **Component:** elimtiyaz-desktop — `src/app/**`, `src/features/**`, `src/shared/**` (the UI layers), `src/i18n/**` (the dictionaries), `src/app/providers/user-preferences-provider.tsx` (AppLocale = "fr" | "ar"), `src/i18n/language-switcher.tsx` (2 hardcoded options + hardcoded French labels "Changer de langue"/"Langue"), `index.html` + `src/index.css` + `tailwind.config.cjs` (the Noto Sans Arabic CDN font)
- **Evidence (the T-388 AST scan, 2026-09-17 — scripts/i18n/scan-hardcoded-strings.mjs, the T-385 portal scanner ported to the desktop with the toast-API surface added; report frozen in scripts/i18n/hardcoded-strings-report.json):** 3,643 findings / 174 files. By kind: 1,973 jsx-text, 440 attr:label, 203 call:showSuccess (+128 templates), 160 attr:title, 149 attr:placeholder, 136 call:showError, 132 jsx-ternary, 93 attr:description, 60 call:showWarning, 34 attr:hint, 32 jsx-fallback, 17 aria-label, … . Deduped (scripts/i18n/collect-unique-strings.mjs): 2,924 unique texts; 1,176 latin-only (English-source); 158 carry template interpolations; 72 map onto EXISTING dictionary keys (e.g. "Modifier" → common.edit) but render hardcoded anyway; the `ar.ts` header itself says "only a subset of strings is provided for now to verify RTL layout works end-to-end". Additional hand findings: the ar app-name value "الإمتiaz" is a corrupted mixed-script string (must be "الإمتياز"); the language switcher's own labels are hardcoded French; `fallbackLng: "fr"` shows raw French for every missing ar key.
- **Root cause:** the desktop predates the i18n discipline — react-i18next was wired early (splash/login/nav/common/auth/dashboard keys) but feature growth never passed through a localization gate, and NO tooling existed on this repo to detect the gap (the T-385 scanner + burn-down guard landed in the WEBSITE repo only). The 3-language mandate was executed against "the portal" reading of the codebase; the desktop module inside the hub repo was never scanned.
